entries.title: Character Types
entries.summary: Introduces the three kinds of player character: magi, companions and grogs. Most players keep more than one character, played according to what the saga needs.

entries.title: Character Templates
entries.summary: Explains that ready-made grog, companion and magus templates give the quickest way to start, and that they can be customized or replaced by detailed creation.

entries.title: Detailed Character Creation
entries.summary: Begins the from-scratch character creation process by choosing a concept for a magus, companion or grog.

entries.title: Detailed Character Creation Summary
entries.summary: Numbered checklist for building a character: concept, House, Virtues and Flaws, Characteristics, early childhood, later life, apprenticeship and later years for magi, Personality, Reputation, Confidence and equipment, with differences between grogs, companions and magi.
quotes: Minor Virtues and Flaws are worth one point, Major Virtues and Flaws three points each.
Start with 7 points.
Take 120 levels of spells, of no higher level than Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory +3.

entries.title: Starting Character Age
entries.summary: Guidance on choosing starting ages: older characters are stronger but take longer to build and must make aging rolls, new players should make recently graduated magi, and companions should be fairly young.
quotes: a character over the age of 35 must make aging rolls

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws at Character Creation
entries.summary: How Virtues and Flaws are allotted by character type: everyone takes a Social Status, grogs get a few minor points with extra limits, and companions and magi may balance Flaws against Virtues. Magi must have The Gift and should take at least one Hermetic Flaw.
quotes: They may have up to three points of Flaws, and a corresponding number of Virtues.
Like companions, magi may take up to ten points of Flaws, and the same number of points of Virtues.

related.text: ArM5 p.61 Virtues and Flaws chapter
ArM5 p.65 Social Statuses by Culture

entries.title: Choosing Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Advice on picking Virtues and Flaws, including the two cases where a Virtue is essential: access to Academic, Arcane, Martial or Supernatural Abilities, and a Social Status such as Knight.
quotes: One is that a character must have a Virtue to buy Academic, Arcane, Martial, or Supernatural Abilities at character creation.

entries.title: Buying Characteristics
entries.summary: Characteristics are bought from a fixed pool of points using a cost table, with negative scores returning points. Magi are advised to value Intelligence and Stamina.
quotes: Characteristics are bought on the following table. You start with seven points to spend.

entries.title: Abilities at Character Creation
entries.summary: Abilities are acquired in blocks: early childhood, later life, and for magi apprenticeship and years afterward. A character's age caps the score in any Ability at creation, though some Virtues raise this.
quotes: Your character's age determines the maximum score she can have in any Ability at character creation, although some Virtues raise this limit.

entries.title: Later Life
entries.summary: After early childhood a character gains experience points each year to spend on Abilities the Virtues allow, with more for the Wealthy Virtue and fewer for the Poor Flaw.
quotes: After early childhood, the character gains 15 experience points per year

entries.title: Personality
entries.summary: Creation step for choosing Personality Traits with scores that match any Personality Flaws; grogs need Loyal and warriors Brave.
quotes: Choose a few words to describe your character's personality, and attach a value between -3 and +3 to each.

entries.title: Quick and Easy Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Simplified shortcut recipes of Virtues and Flaws for grogs, several kinds of companion and for magi, for building characters quickly.
quotes: Take a Minor Personality Flaw that reflects how you want to play the character.

entries.title: Option: Extremely Complex Character Generation
entries.summary: An optional method of building a character by working out what he did in every season of his life using the Laboratory and Long-Term Events rules, which takes far longer.
quotes: However, age-based limits on Abilities do not apply, and all Virtues and Flaws have their normal effect on character advancement.

entries.title: Confidence at Character Creation
entries.summary: Creation step for Confidence: grogs have none, and companions and magi start with a Confidence Score and Points unless a Virtue or Flaw changes them.
quotes: Grogs do not have Confidence Points.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws Basics
entries.summary: How Virtues and Flaws are bought and balanced: Virtues cost points, Flaws grant them, Minor and Major sizes, the cap on Flaws for a central character, and what makes a Flaw acceptable to the troupe.
quotes: Major Virtues cost three points, while Major Flaws grant three points.
A central character may have up to ten points of Flaws, but no more than five Minor Flaws.

entries.title: Virtue and Flaw Limits
entries.summary: General limits on taking Virtues and Flaws: repeats only when allowed, one Social Status, and guidelines for Story and Personality Flaws.
quotes: A Virtue or Flaw may be taken more than once only if the description explicitly allows it.
A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw.

entries.title: Personality Flaws
entries.summary: Guidance on Major and Minor Personality Flaws, including how they drive stories, how often they may be ignored, and limits on how many a character takes.
quotes: A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw
Most characters should not have more than two Personality Flaws, Major or Minor

entries.title: Story Flaws
entries.summary: Story Flaws are external hooks that drag a character into stories; limited to one per character and must depend on something outside the character.
quotes: You should not take more than one Story Flaw, Major or Minor

entries.title: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws are tied to one of the four realms, which governs interaction with auras and grants immunity to Warping from a high aura of the same realm.
quotes: a character with a Supernatural Virtue or Flaw is immune to Warping caused by living in a high aura associated with the same realm

entries.title: Personality and Story Flaw Frequency
entries.summary: Advice for storyguides on limiting Major Personality and Story Flaws so that each has a chance to appear in play.

entries.title: Social Status Requirement
entries.summary: Every character must have a Social Status Virtue or Flaw to show how society sees them, usually limited to the society of the saga; some statuses are restricted by how society perceives the character's gender.
quotes: every character must have one of these, to represent the way that society sees them

entries.title: Social Status Types
entries.summary: Social Status Virtues and Flaws set a character's place in society, and some are Free and cost no points.
quotes: Some Social Status Virtues are Free, which means that they do not cost any points to buy.

entries.title: Social Statuses by Culture
entries.summary: Explains that available Social Statuses depend on culture and lists, per culture, which Free, Minor and Major Virtues and Flaws are available.
quotes: Free Virtues
Hermetic Magus

entries.title: The Gift (Virtue Type)
entries.summary: Describes The Gift as a cost-free Virtue with its penalties, how it lets a character learn Supernatural Abilities and Hermetic Magic, and who should be allowed to have it.
quotes: The Gift is a special Virtue, because it has no cost.

entries.title: Specializations
entries.summary: Each Ability except Spell Mastery gets a specialization that raises the effective score when the specialization applies.
quotes: you act as if your score were one level higher than it actually is

entries.title: Ability Types
entries.summary: Lists the six types of Ability and notes that they are used alike, the difference being who may learn them.
quotes: There are six types of Ability

entries.title: General Abilities (type)
entries.summary: General Abilities can be learned by almost anyone with no game restrictions.
quotes: there are no game restrictions on who may do so

entries.title: Academic Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Academic Abilities need formal training, a Virtue or magus status for beginning characters, and usually a minimum score in a learned language.
quotes: Academic Abilities require formal training.
learning an Academic Knowledge normally requires a Latin, Greek, Hebrew, or Arabic score of at least 3

entries.title: Arcane Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Arcane Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or as a magus, and some Virtues also allow Penetration.
quotes: A character may only take these Abilities during character generation if permitted to by a Virtue, or if he is a magus.

entries.title: Martial Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Martial Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or Flaw, or as a magus.
quotes: Characters may only gain Martial Abilities during character generation if they are permitted to do so by a particular Virtue or Flaw, or if they are magi.

entries.title: Living Languages
entries.summary: Language Abilities measure how well a character communicates, with the lower score of two speakers setting the quality of conversation, penalties for related languages or dialects, and a table of fluency levels.
quotes: When two people speak to each other, the lower Ability score determines how well they communicate.

entries.title: Languages of France and Mutual Comprehension
entries.summary: Lists the Living Languages of France and their dialects (taken as Ability specialties), and gives comprehension penalties when speakers of related languages or dialects talk to each other, with a worked example.
quotes: –1 penalty to both speakers
–2 penalty to both speakers
–3 penalty (only –2 if Frisian dialect) to both speakers

entries.title: Languages of the Nile and Dialect Penalties
entries.summary: Lists the living languages and dialects of Egypt, Nubia and Ethiopia (dialects as specialties), and gives a table of penalties applied to both speakers when related languages or dialects meet.
quotes: Mahasi is on the verge of separating into a separate language, and those who know this dialect have a larger penalty than usual when talking to speakers of the other Nubian dialects.

entries.title: Dead Languages of the Nile
entries.summary: Describes the dead languages Ancient Egyptian, Demotic, Meroitic and Ge'ez, how they relate to living tongues, and their scripts.

entries.title: Sigils
entries.summary: Every maga has a wizard's sigil that appears in her spells and enchantments, never needing requisites and never useful or crippling, and a separate voting sigil for Tribunal.
quotes: Whatever the form of the sigil, it never requires requisites, as it is part of the maga's magic.

entries.title: Creating Creatures
entries.summary: Advice for storyguides designing creatures: start from a concept and role, then choose Might, combat statistics and power costs to suit the intended challenge.
quotes: A Might Score of 20 indicates that starting magi will have a lot of trouble affecting the creature with magic.

entries.title: Dressing As A Man
entries.summary: The simplest way for a woman to avoid social conventions: dressing as a man, which may become a Dark Secret and may qualify for Gender Nonconforming.
quotes: This may become a Dark Secret (page 124), and may also qualify the character for Gender Nonconforming (page 131).

entries.title: Alternative Characters (Troupe Style)
entries.summary: Each player has two or more characters, at least one a magus and one a companion, but plays only one per session, so the characters need good reasons not to adventure together.
quotes: In this version of troupe-style play each player has two or more characters, but only plays one of them in a given session.

entries.title: Writing Systems and Artes Liberales
entries.summary: Explains that a character's Artes Liberales score also limits how many writing systems he can read and write, lists the writing systems of Mythic Europe, and describes how new systems are learned from a source.
quotes: Each point of a character's Artes Liberales score allows him to use one writing system, defined as a separate alphabet and script as well as a separate language.

entries.title: Flaws Representing Malformations
entries.summary: List of Minor and Major Flaws that stand in for malformations in game terms.

entries.title: Make Your Own Plague
entries.summary: Guidance for building a new disease or a disease-causing spell: pick symptoms, translate them into penalties or Flaws, then derive severity, interval and Ease Factors.

entries.title: Calculating the Severity of a Disease
entries.summary: Procedure for working out a disease's Severity from its base level plus Interval and Ease Factor modifiers, with a worked example.
quotes: The Improvement Ease Factor must always be greater than the Stable Ease Factor.

entries.title: Converting Characters
entries.summary: Lets an existing character trade experience in an Academic Ability for formulae of the matching type.
quotes: Every 5 experience points removed from a character's total grants one formula of the appropriate type.

entries.title: Income Bands (Trivial to Legendary)
entries.summary: Defines the six bands of annual profit (Trivial, Minor, Lesser, Typical, Greater, Legendary), what each means as spending money after expenses, example enterprises, and which Social Status Virtues buy each band.
quotes: The income figure listed below for each band is the amount of money a character in that band could spend frivolously in a year without damaging his source of income.
A single workshop, in an average craft, earns 10 Mythic Pounds for its owner each year.

entries.title: Agents
entries.summary: Agents are specialists placed away from the covenant as sources of information or remote help; they are bought with build points but their wages are folded into the general budget unless there are unusually many.
quotes: they need not be included in the covenfolk roster when it comes to determining finances

versions.title: Agents
versions.summary: Defines agents as directly controlled subordinates, gives the formula for how many a principal may have, and lists who does not count as an agent (magi, colorful characters, indirect subordinates, hirelings and other players' characters). A principal with weak Presence or Leadership can run a network through a single primary agent, called a factor.
quotes: 2 x (Presence + Intrigue or Leadership – social penalty for the Gift) or 1, whichever is larger.

entries.title: Design of Agents
entries.summary: The handful of statistics each agent needs: a name, a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, a Bond expressed as a Personality Trait, and the resources the principal can draw on through the agent. Worked examples show how a vassal and a bishop are built.
quotes: A Bond, which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason for the agent's attachment to the principal, and its strength.

entries.title: Acquiring Agents
entries.summary: How characters gain agents, either at character creation through certain Virtues or in play by impressing a prospect with a Presence + Leadership roll and then wearing down his resistance with Agency Experience points. Includes the recruitment, task and persuasion tables.
quotes: Each of these virtues grants 12 points to spend on the accompanying Agent Recruitment Table for thematically appropriate agents.
a stress die + Presence + Leadership – social penalty for the Gift against an Ease Factor of 6.
A character's resistance is reduced by 1 in exchange for a number of Agency experience points equal to their current resistance.

entries.title: Agent Recruitment Table
entries.summary: Tables that set a potential agent's starting resistance from his Social Status, then adjust it for circumstances such as inconvenient Flaws and for the resources he can offer the principal.
quotes: A potential agent always has a minimum resistance score of 1.

entries.title: Designing Agents
entries.summary: Lists the few statistics needed for each agent (name, Social Status, Bond, resources) and the Difficult Underlings problem when a principal controls an agent of higher social standing, with magi exempt.
quotes: A Bond , which is a Personality Trait that expresses the reason that the agent is subordinate to the principal

entries.title: Partial Adoption (Agencies)
entries.summary: Optional approach in which troupes do not convert Virtues and Flaws such as Social Contacts or Close Family Ties into fully described agencies, tracking only agents gained during play.

entries.title: Recruiting Agents at Character Creation
entries.summary: Lists the Virtues and Flaws that grant an agency at the start of play and explains how to buy agents with agency points from the Resistance of Agents Table.
quotes: The player has 12 agency points to spend.

entries.title: Resistance of Agents Table
entries.summary: Tables of base Resistance by Social Status and the modifiers for Flaws, coercion and useful resources, used to cost agents at creation and to set the difficulty of recruiting them. A minimum applies.
quotes: A potential agent's Resistance cannot be less than 1.

entries.title: A Noble Saga
entries.summary: Describes a saga built on a noble household where the lord and a few select staff are companions and everyone else, including his sons of age, are grogs because they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.
quotes: Even the baron's sons who have reached their majority could be considered grog characters, since they are not yet powerful enough to attract Story Flaws.

entries.title: Training Packages
entries.summary: A quick way to build a character's Abilities by stacking packages of years and experience points, working like childhood packages, with limits on repeats, Ability scores and age.
quotes: A starting character should not be built with more than 15 years in a single package

entries.title: The System in Action (Training Packages)
entries.summary: A worked example of building a grog from childhood and training packages, including the effect of the Poor Flaw on age and the 30-or-older Ability cap, followed by sample package combinations for common grog types.
quotes: Since Sir Edwin has taken the Poor Flaw, he is actually 31 years old.

entries.title: Designing a Family
entries.summary: How a player may pick or randomly generate siblings and bastards for a noble character, set their birth order, and roll each sibling's Loyal Personality Trait toward the head of the family. Explains how primogeniture and military inclination change those loyalty results.
quotes: roll two dice of different colors and halve each result
The maximum score is 3 and negative scores are permitted.

entries.title: Profession Herald
entries.summary: A new Profession Ability covering knowledge of the tournament circuit, heraldic devices, colors and deeds, tournament law, and locating tournaments in an area known by Area Lore.
quotes: The Ability Profession: Herald allows a character to recognize knights by their colors and heraldic devices

entries.title: The Manor: The Model Fief
entries.summary: Defines the manor as the basic game unit of fief, the land needed to support a knight and household, and lists what a typical manor contains.
quotes: A manor, for the purposes of the game, comprises the amount of land traditionally required to maintain a knight, his family, and his household retainers.

related.text: LoM Chapter Three: A Comparison of Titles

entries.title: How Big is a…?
entries.summary: Reference sizes and incomes for acres, manors, hides, virgates, bovates, cottars, villages, towns and cities, with the typical split of peasant holdings and a Terram magic scale for an acre of earth.
quotes: For the sake of simplicity an acre is considered to be 4,840 square yards.
A landed knight's income from a typical manor is twenty pounds per year
Twenty percent have a full virgate, thirty percent have a bovate, and fifty percent are cottars.

entries.title: Farmland
entries.summary: The six legal statuses a piece of land can have and the main land types on a heavily farmed manor.
quotes: Each piece of land has one of six legal statuses.

entries.title: Discuss Poverty in Your Saga
entries.summary: Optional guidance for the troupe on how realistic the saga's treatment of peasant hardship, noble villainy and Church oppression should be, including simply choosing a covenant's peasants to be happy at creation.
quotes: Troupes should discuss this and choose a degree of realism that suits the stories they wish to tell.

entries.title: New Abilities
entries.summary: Defines the Abilities Profession Sapper, Profession Siege Engineer and Siege Weapon, with what each covers and suggested specialities.
quotes: This Ability may not be used untrained

entries.title: Melee Weapon Table
entries.summary: Consolidated table of melee weapons and shields with Ability, Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Strength, Load, Cost, availability, damage type and damage levels, with notes on nets, whips, long swords and polearms.
quotes: A net or whip may be used to trip, grapple, or disarm using wielder's Single Weapon + Weapon Attack Bonus in lieu of Brawl.
A halberd or pole arm may be used to unseat a rider.

entries.title: Missile Weapon Table
entries.summary: Consolidated table of thrown and missile weapons, bows and crossbows with Ability, Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Range, Strength, Load, Cost, availability and damage type.
quotes: | Arbalest | Crossbow | 5 | 5 | 0 | 10 | 30 | –1 | 3 | Exp. | High | P | 2 | New |

entries.title: Armor Materials
entries.summary: The expanded armor material categories replace those in the core rules while remaining compatible with their statistics.
quotes: The following categories expand and supersede those described on page 176 of ArM5.

entries.title: Inexpensive Materials
entries.summary: Defines padded armor and boiled leather as the inexpensive armor material categories, and which similar materials use the same statistics.
quotes: Also use these statistics for similar, semiresilient materials like rawhide, or even faerie armor made of tree bark.

entries.title: Standard Materials
entries.summary: Defines reinforced armor, rigid scale and metal scale as the standard armor material categories.
quotes: Metal scale includes all kinds of metal lamellar.

entries.title: Weapon Table Key
entries.summary: Explains each column of the melee and missile weapon tables, including untrained weapon use, minimum Strength, Load, cost, availability, damage types and damage levels.
quotes: add three extra botch dice unless the weapon is a crossbow

entries.title: Expensive Materials
entries.summary: Defines mail, plate, and plate and mail as the expensive armor material categories, with notes on when each appeared historically and that the complex armor rules do not cover 15th-century full plate.
quotes: The complex armor design rules do not cover 15th-century full plate.

entries.title: Expanded Armor Table
entries.summary: Tables giving Protection and Load for each armor material in each garment type, plus surcoats, greaves and helmets, which are added together to get a character's total Protection and Load.
quotes: Retain fractions until the end of the calculation and then round up to the next whole number.

entries.title: Glossary of Armor Terms
entries.summary: Definitions of armor terms such as hauberk, haubergeon, cuirass, jerkin, gambeson and brigandine, used to read the armor tables, with a few notes on which statistics to use for certain armors.
quotes: Use the statistics for a metal scale cuirass.

entries.title: Option: Complex Armor Design
entries.summary: Optional procedure for designing armor from any combination of materials: for each material add the Protection of the body areas it covers, multiply by the material's Load Factor, then sum all materials and round up.
quotes: multiply it by the Load Factor for that material and retain any fraction to get the total Load of that material

entries.title: Complex Armor Design Table
entries.summary: Table giving, for each armor material, the Protection it provides on each body area and its Load Factor, for use with the complex armor design procedure.

entries.title: Clergy as Player Characters
entries.summary: Clergy characters are built as ordinary grogs or companions under the standard character rules; the sidebar lists ways clergy can be tied into a covenant saga.

entries.title: Vows
entries.summary: Guidance on how to represent a Church character's vows at character creation: the Monastic Vows Story Flaw only if the troupe wants vow-driven stories, a suitable Personality Flaw or Regular otherwise, or simply a note with no Virtue or Flaw.

entries.title: Recommended and Required Virtues, Flaws, and Abilities
entries.summary: A table of the Virtues and Flaws required and recommended, and the minimum Ability scores suggested, for popes, cardinals and archbishops; for bishops, abbots and senior officials; and for ordinary clergy.
quotes: Recommended Minimum Ability Scores: Artes Liberales 1, Church Lore 5, Civil and Canon Law 5, Dead Language: Latin 5, Theology 3.

entries.title: Becoming a Monk or Nun
entries.summary: The procedure for entering a religious house: harsh testing on arrival, a probationary year as a novice, the three solemn vows, and rules on oblates and the admission of girls to nunneries.
quotes: The three chief vows that are sworn as solemn oaths are for chastity, poverty, and obedience.

entries.title: The Religious in Your Saga
entries.summary: Advice on playing a monk or nun in a saga: limited free seasons outside the house, how religious roles bring them into the wider world, and the economic importance of monasteries and their hospitality to travellers.
quotes: even the most trusted monk may seem unlikely to have more than one free season outside the monastery each year

entries.title: Female Religious in the Covenant
entries.summary: When a female religious character may live at a covenant: beguines, penitents and anchoresses need the bishop's permission, a nun needs a harder petition, episcopal visits must be managed, and vows and Flaws should reflect the character's way of life.
quotes: a Petition Ease Factor of 9 is appropriate
the Petition Ease Factor is 12

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church
The Lion and the Lily p.106 Cunfin

entries.title: Options for Absent Players
entries.summary: Suggests using an enclosed religious or anchoress character for a player who cannot attend sessions, with ways of passing letters between the cell and the covenant.

entries.title: Converting Characters from Fourth Edition The Mysteries
entries.summary: Notes for converting Fourth Edition Mysteries characters: Abilities, Virtues and Flaws, Mastery, Mystae magics and the new Revised Edition schools.
quotes: Mastery Virtues are replaced by Mastery special abilities; see ArM5, page 87.
adding one Mastery Level for each Ability added

entries.title: Covenant Boons and Hooks (aligned auras)
entries.summary: Additional covenant-creation Boons and Hooks based on an aura alignment: Fine Aura, Favorable Aura and Troublesome Aura.
quotes: Fine Aura: The Magic aura of the covenant has an alignment that benefits most of those within it.

entries.title: Hungarian Social Classes as Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Maps each Hungarian social class (serfs, castle folk, hospites, castle warriors, free horsemen, petty and greater nobles, counts, bishops) to the Virtues and Flaws used to build such a character, with the seasons, money and retainers a landed noble gets.
quotes: Serfs, udvornici, most free men, and castle folk use the Peasant Free Virtue.
A Landed Noble, lacking other Virtues or Flaws, spends two seasons a year on maintaining his lifestyle, with a spare 10 pounds a year for largesse.
Counts must take the Oath of Fealty Flaw.

entries.title: Founding a Covenant in the Rhine Tribunal
entries.summary: Explains the Rhine Tribunal's rule that a new covenant needs the approval of every existing covenant before it is recognized, the consequences of lacking recognition, the bargaining and gift-giving that follow, and the sidebar ruling that requires a sponsor from each covenant.
quotes: prospective covenants have been required to obtain the explicit permission of all the Tribunal's other covenants, in order to obtain recognition
If a covenant is not successful in getting approval from the Tribunal, they may try again in seven years time.

entries.title: Rhine Tribunal Ranks
entries.summary: Introduces the four ranks by which the Rhine Tribunal classes its magi: apprentice, journeyman, master and archmage.
quotes: The Rhine Tribunal has four recognized ranks by which it classes its members.

entries.title: Rhine Journeyman Rank
entries.summary: Explains how a magus becomes a journeyman (tyro) at Durenmar after the Gauntlet, receiving a voting sigil and the option to declare for a gild, and the choices of founding a covenant, joining one, or wandering as a peregrinator.
quotes: The magus is now legally a journeyman, and he may declare membership of a gild, if he wishes.

related.text: Laws of Hospitality and the Peregrinatores

entries.title: The Gild System
entries.summary: Explains how the Rhine Tribunal's political gilds work: joining is open and public, members are expected to vote with the gild, gild members can call on each other for help and are protected from Wizard War by their fellows, and leaving or being expelled carries a social price.
quotes: Nevertheless, the Oath of Hermes forbids any mechanism to coerce a magus to vote in a particular way
All gilds forbid Wizard War among their members
Those that do not do so within seven years of their Gauntlet or their arrival in the Tribunal generally acquire a reputation as a loner.

entries.title: Establishing Your Covenant: Four Starting Options
entries.summary: Sets out four ways a group of Rhine magi can begin a saga: founding a new covenant, establishing a chapter house, settling at an existing covenant, or travelling between covenants as peregrinatores. Each option carries different approval requirements, resources and independence.
quotes: Any covenant with sufficient resources might support chapters

related.text: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, On the Founding of Covenants

entries.title: Saga Start: A Gentle Introduction
entries.summary: An easier saga start in which an existing friendly covenant supplies labs, books, grogs, vis or money while the young magi explore before settling.

entries.title: Saga Start: In at the Deep End
entries.summary: A harder saga start in which the magi leave Durenmar lightly equipped with scant resources and must found the covenant from the ground up.

entries.title: Seeking Tribunal Approval for a New Covenant
entries.summary: Rhine law requires a prospective covenant to be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant, which usually means trading promises, favors and debts; the sponsorship of a single magus is enough from each covenant.
quotes: a prospective covenant must be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant in the Tribunal

related.text: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, On the Founding of Covenants

entries.title: Peregrinatores: Travelling Between Covenants
entries.summary: The Rhine Tribunal's tradition of hospitality lets wandering magi guest at other covenants without a permanent home of their own.
quotes: traditions of hospitality for wandering magi

related.text: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

entries.title: Languages in Germany and Mutual Intelligibility
entries.summary: Lists the Living Languages of Germany with their dialect specialties and gives penalties applied when speakers of related languages or dialects try to understand each other, with a worked example.
quotes: Same language, different dialects: –1 penalty to both speakers
High German vs Low German: –2 penalty to both speakers
High German vs East Norse or English: –4 penalty to both speakers

entries.title: Pretending to Be Male or Married (Dark Secrets)
entries.summary: Advice on when a female character's disguise as a man or as a married woman counts as a Dark Secret or Gender Nonconforming Flaw, and when it is only a convenience.
quotes: If it will ruin the character's life, it is a Dark Secret.

entries.title: Magi Only: Hermetic House
entries.summary: Choosing a House is the next step in creating a magus, and each House grants a particular benefit at creation. A magus can belong to only one House.

entries.title: Hermetic Houses Summary
entries.summary: A table of each House with its type, a short description and the benefit it grants at character creation, such as a free Virtue or Mystery.

related.text: ArM5 p.12 The Houses of Hermes

entries.title: Hermetic Magi Recommended Minimum Abilities
entries.summary: A recommended minimum Ability set for new magi and the rule that the highest spell level a magus can learn at creation is limited by an Art-based total.
quotes: The highest level spell you can learn is equal to Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory +3

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Magi
entries.summary: Character-creation limits for magi: balanced Virtues and Flaws, at most one Major Hermetic Virtue, required Gift and Hermetic Magus status, and a free House Minor Virtue.
quotes: You must take The Gift and the Hermetic Magus Social Status Virtue
You may not have more than one Major Hermetic Virtue

entries.title: Hermetic Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Only characters with The Gift can take Hermetic Virtues and Flaws; a troupe may let a character with many Supernatural Virtues take Hermetic Flaws as Supernatural Flaws.
quotes: Only characters with The Gift can take these Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: The Hermetic Arts
entries.summary: Explains that magi have a score in each Technique and Form, that a spell combines one of each, and that a Form score gives a Form Bonus to resist related hazards (bonuses do not stack).
quotes: FORM BONUS: Form score/5 (rounded up)
These bonuses do not stack.

entries.title: Hermetic Books: Definition of Categories of Value
entries.summary: Sidebar giving typical Quality ranges for summae and tractatus (excellent, sound, vain, discarded and legendary books) as a function of Level.
quotes: These Summae have a Quality of (25 – Level) or below.

entries.title: A Redcap Saga
entries.summary: Explains that the Redcap Virtue is normally unavailable to grogs because it is a Major Social Status Virtue, and offers two fixes: make it a free Virtue for all characters or have the player characters work for redcaps instead.
quotes: allow the Redcap Virtue as a free Virtue

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages ch.3

entries.title: After the Arts Are Opened
entries.summary: Once Opened, an apprentice has score 0 in every Art, can cast spontaneous spells and read casting tablets with the right Abilities, and uses the standard magical formulas with current Arts.
quotes: Once the Arts are Opened, the apprentice character has a 0 in each of the five Techniques and ten Forms.

entries.title: Learning Parma Magica
entries.summary: An apprentice accumulates Parma Magica experience through exposure but cannot invoke it until the final key instruction is given after swearing the Oath of Hermes; teaching it earlier is a High Crime.
quotes: Usually, an apprentice character finishes apprenticeship with a score of 1 in Parma Magica.
doing so before the apprentice swears the Oath of Hermes is a High Crime

entries.title: Saga Magi: Characters and Starting Resources
entries.summary: Guidance for building the player magi for the Curse of the Rhine Gorge saga: backgrounds, optional Gild Trained for Rhine-apprenticed magi, and a spread of starting resources such as shield grogs and money, with Fengheld magi favored.
quotes: the Minor Virtue (Gild) Trained
which allows them to start with a personal shield grog and a reasonable sum of money

related.text: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

entries.title: Companions
entries.summary: Companions are important non-magi who belong to one player. They normally lack The Gift and should be linked to another player's magus rather than to their own.
quotes: Companions should generally not have The Gift, unless you intend to play through apprenticeship so that they become magi at some point.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Companions
entries.summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for companions, including Minor Flaw limits and Social Status requirement.
quotes: You may take up to 10 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not have more than 5 Minor Flaws

entries.title: Companions for the Saga
entries.summary: Suggests companion character types that magi may befriend as the covenant settles in, and advises making a player's companion dissimilar to their magus.
quotes: these two characters should ideally be dissimilar

entries.title: Grogs
entries.summary: Grogs are minor, often shared characters, usually built from templates or detailed creation with limits: no Major Virtues or Flaws, no Story Flaws, and never The Gift.
quotes: grogs can never have The Gift

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Grogs
entries.summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for grogs, including bans on Major Virtues and Flaws, Hermetic Virtues and The Gift.
quotes: You may take up to 3 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not take Major Virtues or Flaws

entries.title: Companions vs. Grogs for Craftsmen
entries.summary: Clarifies that companion and grog status depends on narrative role rather than craft rank, while the Virtue and Flaw limits for each type still apply.
quotes: Companions and grogs are defined by their narrative role

entries.title: The Sample Characters (Grog Template Limits)
entries.summary: Guidelines for building grogs: no Major Virtues or Flaws, at most three Minor Flaws balanced by an equal number of Minor Virtues, no Story Flaws, and normally no more than one Minor Personality Flaw. Templates should include Covenant Lore and Village Lore.
quotes: Grogs should have no Major Virtues or Flaws, no more than three Minor Flaws balanced by an equal number of Minor Virtues, and no Story Flaws.

entries.title: Starting Characteristics
entries.summary: Table of ready-made arrays of eight Characteristic scores bought with the standard number of points, from which a player can simply pick one for a grog.

entries.title: Characteristics (grog creation)
entries.summary: Grogs buy Characteristics with the standard point pool, optionally taking negative points for more, or choose a pre-made array from the Starting Characteristics table.
quotes: Every character has 7 points to spend on buying positive Characteristics

entries.title: Aging, the Easy Way
entries.summary: A shortcut for aging old or many characters by looking up the Aging Points gained per decade for mild, average or harsh aging at the character's Aging Score, with a simple-die method to find Apparent Age.
quotes: age/10 (round up) – Living Conditions modifier – Longevity Ritual modifier

entries.title: Aging Chart
entries.summary: Table of expected Aging Points and crises per decade by Aging Score for mild, average and harsh aging, excluding points from crises.
quotes: The Aging Points listed exclude those deriving from crises.

entries.title: Applying Crises
entries.summary: Optional use of the crises listed on the Aging Chart: the character gains a Decrepitude score equal to the crises and additional Aging Points that shrink by fraction with each extra crisis, rounded up.
quotes: if he suffers one crisis, then he gets half of the Aging Points listed in the Aging Chart

entries.title: Effects of Aging on Characteristics
entries.summary: Gives the approximate distribution of Aging Points among Characteristics so they can be applied in line with the Aging Table.
quotes: The Aging Table (ArM5, page 170) is designed to affect certain Characteristics in favor of others.

entries.title: Childhood Training Packages
entries.summary: Lists the core childhood packages in training-package format plus two new ones, Covenant-bred and Feral, each granting experience in Abilities for the first years of life.
quotes: These packages can only be taken for the first five years of life.

entries.title: Personality Traits for grogs
entries.summary: Suggests troupes make greater use of Personality Trait rolls for grogs, gives the usual starting Traits (Brave and Loyal), and says a Personality Flaw can be matched with an extra Trait at a set value.
quotes: Most grogs should have a Brave and a Loyal Personality Trait.
This trait should have a value of +3 (for a Minor Flaw) or +6 (for a Major Flaw).

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws (changing them over time)
entries.summary: Characters can change their Virtues and Flaws over time; established characters may swap a Minor for a Minor or a Major for a Major with troupe approval, without touching Characteristics or Abilities or a feature of earlier stories.
quotes: a Minor Flaw can be exchanged for another Minor Flaw, and a Major Flaw for a Major Flaw, and the same applies to Virtues

entries.title: Gaining New Flaws
entries.summary: Characters can gain Flaws through misfortune or action, but changed circumstances only become a Flaw when they affect the game, and grogs should not gain Story Flaws unless temporary or heading for transformation.
quotes: The storyguide should be careful not to allow a grog character to gain a Story Flaw

entries.title: Changes in Social Status
entries.summary: When a character's standing changes, such as promotion to custos or taking Holy Orders, the old Social Status Virtue or Flaw is simply replaced by the new one except where its description says both are kept.
quotes: simply replace the old Social Status Virtue with the new one

entries.title: Gaining Flaws Through Mishaps
entries.summary: General Flaws, especially physical ones, are most often gained through misfortune such as amputations, battlefield injuries and diseases.
quotes: Most often, General Flaws are gained through mishap, particularly those that affect the body.

entries.title: Gaining Flaws Through Actions
entries.summary: Actions can change social status or, with the storyguide's approval, bring Story Flaws such as a feud or debt, though grogs are usually barred from Story Flaws during play as in creation; offending a faerie can bring a Malediction or disfigurement.
quotes: although grogs are usually prohibited from gaining Story Flaws during the game

entries.title: Gaining Flaws Through Magic
entries.summary: Curses from hedge wizard traditions are usually limited in duration, supernatural creatures can impose permanent Flaws at a cost to their Might, and Warping gives Flaws to characters not aligned to a Realm.
quotes: Warping induces the acquisition of Flaws in those characters who are not aligned to a Supernatural Realm

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.109

entries.title: Gaining New Virtues
entries.summary: New Virtues are gained through magic, initiation or actions; a newly gained Virtue that affects experience does not retroactively change experience already gained.
quotes: this does not affect any experience points gained thus far

entries.title: Gaining Virtues Through Magic
entries.summary: Supernatural sources can grant Virtues temporarily or permanently, such as gruagach spells, Objects of Virtue, faerie wizardry, Goetic Arts and creatures who give up Might; severe Warping can also confer Virtues.
quotes: The acquisition of Virtues in this manner should never be frivolous

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.114

entries.title: Gaining Virtues Through Initiation
entries.summary: Initiation into a mystery cult or hedge tradition grants Virtues after the character builds a score in the relevant Organization Lore and pays through ordeals, quests, sacrifice and study; grogs most commonly are initiated into the Ceremony Ability.
quotes: The character must develop a score in the Organization Lore of the cult or tradition in question before even being considered for Initiation.

entries.title: Gaining Virtues Through Actions
entries.summary: Actions in stories, usually social interaction with storyguide characters, can give the effects of a Virtue such as Social Contacts or Protection, but a grog should be cautious about gaining a Major Virtue.
quotes: The troupe should be cautious about a grog gaining a Major Virtue

entries.title: Losing Flaws
entries.summary: Most methods of gaining Virtues can also remove Flaws, though not every method suits every Flaw, and stories can lift curses.
quotes: Most of the methods by which Virtues can be gained (see earlier) can also rid a character of Flaws

entries.title: Character Transformation (grog to companion)
entries.summary: Explains how a grog can be turned into a companion when a story justifies it, with the troupe ensuring the new Virtues and Flaws suit the transformation and not padding Flaws just for more Virtue points.
quotes: The chief game difference between grogs and companions is the number and type of Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Inauguration
entries.summary: A transformation route in which a character is invested with temporal or spiritual authority and changes social status, such as becoming dean of a guild or a landed noble.
quotes: Those events which result in the investiture of a character with temporal or spiritual authority are termed inaugurations.

entries.title: Metamorphosis
entries.summary: A transformation route in which a magical change permanently turns a character into something else, often granting Supernatural Virtues and Flaws of the relevant realm.
quotes: Metamorphosis often results in the acquisition of Supernatural Virtues and Flaws from the appropriate realm.

entries.title: Initiation (as transformation)
entries.summary: Initiation into a mystery cult can transform a grog into a companion, and is the route most likely to produce a Mythic Companion, a magus-equivalent character.
quotes: initiation is perhaps the most likely to produce a Mythic Companion, which is a magus-equivalent character

entries.title: Pilgrimage (as transformation)
entries.summary: Any story or arc that takes a character out of his routine, tests him and changes his life can serve as a pilgrimage and justify transforming a grog into a companion.
quotes: Any story or story arc that takes a character out of his normal routine and location, tests his character, and then transforms his life forever is a pilgrimage.

entries.title: Grog Backgrounds
entries.summary: Advises giving grogs some years of labor, craft or trade packages before a military package, to generate a simple back story.

entries.title: Combat Statistics (Grogs)
entries.summary: Pre-calculated combat statistics for common weapons under stated assumptions about Ability, Characteristics and encumbrance, to save time when building grogs.
quotes: It is often tedious to calculate combat statistics for a grog.

entries.title: Advisor Grog Template
entries.summary: A character-creation template for a knowledge-specialist covenant retainer, with role notes, suggested Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Abilities, training packages and sample Ability scores at three ages.
quotes: By assigning –1 to each of the four physical Characteristics, scores of +3, +2, +1, and +1 are available to assign to the mental Characteristics.

entries.title: Almogavar Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for Iberian mercenary-raider units, covering their organisation and tactics, how to build an Almogavar character, standard outfit and protection, suggested Virtues, Flaws, Abilities and packages, and sample Ability scores at three ages.
quotes: The combination of sheepskin leather and the open-faced iron helmet grants a Protection of 1, with a Load of 1.

entries.title: Animal Trainer Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for characters who train animals for a covenant, with suggested Abilities, training packages and three sample characters of different ages and backgrounds.

entries.title: Bodyguard Maidservant Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a female grog who serves as a disguised bodyguard and spy, with suggested Virtues, Flaws, Social Status, Abilities, packages and sample Ability scores for a young and a mature character.

entries.title: The Bull Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for the strong, loyal and none-too-clever fighting grog, with suggested Virtues, Flaws, Social Status, Abilities, packages and sample Ability scores at three ages.

entries.title: Confessor Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for the priest or religious counsellor who hears confession for covenfolk and magi, with variants for Christian, Islamic and Jewish characters, suggested Virtues and Flaws, packages and sample Ability scores.

entries.title: Corpse-Thief Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a grave-robbing supplier of arcane connections and body parts to witches, covering the Abilities and sympathetic-connection craft that make him useful, suggested Virtues and Flaws, packages and sample Ability scores.

entries.title: Craftsman Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for the covenant craftsman who may progress from apprentice to master over a saga, with Virtue and Flaw suggestions for each stage, Finesse, packages, sample Ability scores, workshop and assistants rules.

entries.title: Ex-Prostitute Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for women who left the sex trade and joined a covenant, covering how they come to covenants and how to build such a character with suggested Virtues, Flaws, packages and sample Ability scores.

entries.title: Farrier Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a horse-care specialist, with suggested Virtues, Flaws, Social Status, Abilities, packages and sample Ability scores for apprentice, journeyman and master.

entries.title: Jack-of-All-Trades Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a wandering generalist who has picked up many skills, with suggested Flaws explaining why he cannot settle, packages and sample Ability scores at three ages.

entries.title: Misguided Mystic Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a character with genuine or imagined prophetic gifts who misunderstands them, with suggested Supernatural Virtues and Flaws, Abilities, packages and sample Ability scores.

entries.title: Murderer Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for an unrepentant killer who has taken sanctuary in a covenant, with suggested Virtues and Flaws, how the Master of None Flaw alters training packages, Reputation notes and sample Ability scores at three ages.
quotes: He also has a Local Reputation as a murderer.

entries.title: Parent of a Gifted Child Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for the mundane parent of a Gifted apprentice who joins the covenant as a general-purpose grog, with suggested Abilities and sample Ability scores at two ages.

entries.title: Refugee Librarian Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for covenfolk whose covenant has fallen and who seek a new home, including Virtue and Flaw suggestions, packages and sample Ability scores for a trained librarian.

entries.title: Street Thug Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a city gang member who serves as the covenant's contact with the underworld, including how a harsh urban life affects aging, suggested Virtues, Flaws, Abilities, packages and sample Ability scores at three ages.
quotes: the Street Thug can expect to have a Decrepitude Score of 2 and Characteristics totaling –5, rather than the starting 7, by the age of 50

entries.title: Brief Grog Concepts
entries.summary: Short character concepts such as the Accursed, Barbarian, Coward, Hero and Survivor, each with notes on key Abilities, suitable Virtues and Flaws, and which training packages to use.

entries.title: Saga Grogs and Shield Grogs
entries.summary: Explains that grogs are less central than magi, need not be taken at the very start, and may be recruited or donated as a founding gift; a shield grog should be played by someone other than the magus's player.
quotes: A grog who is assigned to be the shield grog of a particular magus should be played by someone other than the player of that magus.

entries.title: Early Childhood
entries.summary: The first five years of life give experience points in the native language and a further pool to split among a fixed list of childhood Abilities.
quotes: In the first five years of life, characters gain 75 experience points in their native language

entries.title: Magus Only - Apprenticeship
entries.summary: A magus's apprenticeship grants experience points to spend on Arts and Abilities and levels of spells, with minimum required Abilities for admission to the Order and warnings about Latin and Magic Theory.
quotes: The fifteen years of apprenticeship give the character 240 experience points, and 120 levels of spells.
Magi must have the following minimum Abilities: Parma Magica 1, Magic Theory 1, Latin 1.

entries.title: Sample Childhoods
entries.summary: Ready-made Ability packages for five types of childhood, to speed up creation.
quotes: Social Childhood: Charm 2, Folk Ken 2, Guile 2, Native Language 5

entries.title: Magus Only - After Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Optional rules for creating a magus who is some years past apprenticeship: yearly points spread across Art and Ability experience and spell levels, a typical lab context, and a reduction for seasons spent on lab projects.
quotes: For every year, the magus gets 30 points.
For each season that your magus spends working on a lab project, the character loses 10 points from the yearly 30 experience points

entries.title: Fleshing Out Your Apprentice
entries.summary: An apprentice adds Intelligence plus Magic Theory to Lab Totals; to play one as a full character, create a young character with The Gift whose Arts the magus can open.

entries.title: Ages of Man
entries.summary: Defines the infant, child and adolescent life stages by age band, and explains that the liminal periods between stages let a player modify the character.
quotes: an infant character is between birth and seven years old, a child character between eight and 14, and an adolescent character between 15 and 21

entries.title: Starting Age for Young Characters
entries.summary: Explains how to choose a young character's starting age, the penalties younger characters suffer, and that starting age also fixes starting experience points.
quotes: Characters younger than 14 have penalties applied to Characteristics and Size

entries.title: Aging Chart (Characteristic and Size Modifiers by Age)
entries.summary: A table giving, for each age, the Characteristic Modifier applied to every Characteristic and the Size Modifier of a young character.
quotes: apply the Characteristic Modifier to all of the character's Characteristics

entries.title: Characteristics and Size for Young Characters
entries.summary: Young characters allocate Characteristic points like adults, then apply the age-based Characteristic and Size modifiers from the Aging Chart.
quotes: younger characters have 7 points allocated toward Characteristics

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Young Characters
entries.summary: Age does not change how many Virtues and Flaws a character may take; they must balance at child character generation, with an exception for apprentices who already have the Free House Virtue.
quotes: At character generation, the number of Virtues must equal the number of Flaws.
Young grogs can have up to three points of Virtues and Flaws, and young companions and apprentices can have up to ten

related.text: ArM5 p.37 Virtues and Flaws Rules and Guidelines

entries.title: Changing Social Status
entries.summary: Sidebar on how a child's Social Status Virtue or Flaw changes during play, and that the change does not require re-balancing other Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: In such cases, simply change the Social Status Virtue or Flaw.

entries.title: Social Status for Young Characters
entries.summary: A child normally takes the Social Status of the parent as Son or Daughter of that status; children without a recognized parent are bastards or orphans, and apprentices take the Apprentice status.
quotes: Every character needs a Social Status Virtue or Flaw.

entries.title: Virtues That Grant Experience Points (and Skilled/Weak Parens)
entries.summary: Experience-granting Virtues are barred for young characters, and Skilled Parens and Weak Parens are given concrete Teaching Source Quality and Lab Total values within a standard apprenticeship.
quotes: a Skilled Parens must generate a Teaching Source Quality of 18, or have a combined Communication + Teaching of 9, and needs a highest applicable Lab Total of 50

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws That Affect Size
entries.summary: How Size-altering Virtues and Flaws apply as a child grows, including how smaller characters stay stunted and when they advance a Size step.
quotes: A normal baby grows to Size 0 by age 14

entries.title: Inherited Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: A new type of Virtue or Flaw that is paid for at creation but only manifests later, by player choice or in response to play; it must appear by adulthood.
quotes: All Inherited Virtues and Flaws must materialize by adulthood (age 21).

entries.title: Child Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: A new type of Virtue and Flaw reflecting childhood boons and banes; they must be exchanged for another of like value during a Transition of Maturation.
quotes: you must exchange the Child Virtue or Flaw for another Virtue or Flaw of like value (Minor for Minor, Major for Major)

entries.title: Abilities for Young Characters
entries.summary: Covers yearly experience points for Abilities by starting age, vocational Abilities limited by the parent's score, Supernatural Abilities for Gifted children, the mid-career apprentice experience model, and age limits on Ability scores.
quotes: After 5 years of age, the character gains 15 experience points a year.
The child character's score is limited to half the parent's vocational Ability score during these years.
The character receives 19 experience points per year of apprenticeship for the first 12 years

related.text: ArM5 p.31 Ability caps by age
ArM5 p.32 spells at character generation

entries.title: Example Childhoods
entries.summary: Sidebar of ready-made Ability packages for the experience points a character has accumulated by age five, to speed up character creation.
quotes: The following Ability packages describe how to spend the 45 experience points a character has accumulated by age 5

entries.title: Optional Rule: Abilities for Infants
entries.summary: Optional rule for characters aged five or younger giving yearly experience points, a fixed part of which must go to a Living Language and the rest to a short list of Abilities.
quotes: he receives 24 experience points per year

entries.title: More Powerful than Normal
entries.summary: Sidebar warning that young Gifted characters advanced season by season can outstrip stock magi, and advising the standard study model to keep power level equal.
quotes: limit them to the standard study model

related.text: ArM5 p.33 Extremely Complex Character Generation

entries.title: Transitions of Maturation
entries.summary: At the ages between life stages the player may exchange Virtues and Flaws for ones of equal value, with restrictions on experience-affecting, Size-affecting and background Virtues and Flaws, and Child Virtues and Flaws must be gone by the last transition.
quotes: Both must be exchanged for Virtues and Flaws of equal value: Minor replaced with Minor and Major replaced with Major.

entries.title: Infant Character Design Notes (Wounds)
entries.summary: Warns that infant characters are extremely fragile and offers two options for damage: trading wounds for Flaws or adding the age modifier penalty to Wound Recovery rolls.
quotes: The second option is add the child character's age modifier penalty to any wound recovery roll that the character needs to make.

related.text: Lords of Men p.125 Option: Mitigating Deadly Wounds

entries.title: A Standard Apprenticeship
entries.summary: A benchmark year-by-year model of a fifteen-year apprenticeship giving the experience points and spell levels an apprentice receives, used to build mid-apprenticeship characters.
quotes: In game terms, the player receives 240 experience points to spend on Abilities and Arts, and 120 levels of spells.
an apprentice gains 19 experience points a year for eleven years of the apprenticeship

entries.title: Becoming an Apprentice
entries.summary: How a found child becomes an apprentice, which Abilities a pre-apprentice child may have, and how an untrained child can help in the laboratory by adding to Safety, Aesthetics and a Mentem Specialty.
quotes: The character adds his Intelligence divided by 2 to a lab's Safety, +1 to Aesthetics, and +1 to a Mentem Specialty

entries.title: Post-Apprenticeship
entries.summary: What a newly Gauntleted magus does next, customary gifts, and the recommended minimum Ability scores, noting that an apprentice is a magus once Opened, trained and passed.
quotes: The recommended minimum Ability scores for a magus are Artes Liberales 1, Latin 4, Magic Theory 3, and Parma Magica 1

entries.title: Playing Gifted Children (Scholomance saga option)
entries.summary: Optional saga premise that starts the player characters as pupils in the same Scholomance class, giving a shared backstory for why a group of magi settle together and who their companions might be.
quotes: Having them as members of the Scholomance's class gives an opportunity for characters of different backgrounds to meet and form friendships.

entries.title: Rhine Apprenticeship and Durenmar Training
entries.summary: Describes the legal status of a Rhine apprentice and the Peripheral Code requirement that every apprentice trained in the Tribunal spend time at Durenmar, including the optional induction into a political gild.
quotes: must spend a minimum of one season learning at Durenmar, to complement their normal studies

entries.title: Personality Traits for the Four Complexions
entries.summary: Lists suggested Personality Traits associated with each of the four complexions, useful when choosing a character's Traits or reading a patient's complexion.

entries.title: Specialties for Medicine
entries.summary: Lists the areas that are suitable as Medicine specialties under the rules in this chapter.
quotes: diagnosis, prognosis, therapy, regimens, theriac, a specific disease

entries.title: Profession Apothecary
entries.summary: Describes the Profession: Apothecary Ability for identifying, growing and preparing medicinal ingredients, and the Medicine penalty when no medicinal supplies are available.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

versions.title: Profession Apothecary
versions.summary: Ability for identifying and preparing medicinal ingredients. Lack of proper medicinal supplies penalizes Medicine rolls and the patient's Recovery bonus, and a skilled apothecary reduces that penalty.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

entries.title: Formally Trained Physician Characters
entries.summary: Character creation guidance for medici, chirurgeons, clerical physicians and apothecaries: when a character may use the titles medicus or doctor and which Social Status and other Virtues and Abilities suit each.
quotes: Anyone with Medicine 1 or greater may call himself a medicus

entries.title: Empiricus Characters
entries.summary: Character creation guidance for empirici, barber-surgeons, midwives and herbwives: suitable Social Status Virtues and Flaws, and how a midwife's removed thumbs are handled.
quotes: If a midwife has had her thumbs removed she effectively has the Palsied Hands Flaw; except in rolls involving childbirth, where she has a +2 bonus instead of the penalty.

entries.title: New Virtues and Flaws (Universities)
entries.summary: Explains how the new university Social Status Virtues work: only one is normally held, it need not be rebalanced as a character advances, every student has benefit of clergy, and the stages from student to doctor each build on the previous Virtue.
quotes: it is not necessary to balance Social Status Virtues after character generation
Every university student receives the benefit of clergy

entries.title: Artists and Artwork (Craft vs. Profession)
entries.summary: Explains how the book splits artists into production artists (who use a Craft Ability) and performance artists (who use a Profession Ability), which free Social Status Virtue each should take, and what counts as artwork (with an Aesthetic Quality) rather than a manufactured item.
quotes: Production artists should take the free Social Status Virtue: Craftsman, and performance artists should take the free Social Status Virtue: Wanderer.
Every piece of artwork has an Aesthetic Quality that determines how beautiful it is.

entries.title: Guild Lore (Ability)
entries.summary: A new Organization Lore Ability covering a guild's rules and bylaws, used for checks about guild members, other guilds and trade matters, with suggested specialties.
quotes: Guild Lore is an (Organization) Lore Ability that covers the rules and bylaws of the guild.

entries.title: Craftsmen (Regular Craftsman Characters)
entries.summary: Rules for non-guild craftsman characters: the free Virtue, the Abilities they need, how many apprentices they may train, and how rural, urban, monastic and covenant craftsmen differ.
quotes: A regular craftsman character must have the Free Social Virtue Craftsman.
Bargain and Craft are the only two mandatory Abilities that an average, non-guild member craftsman character needs.
A regular craftsman may have a number of apprentices at a single time equal to his Leadership score.

entries.title: Laborers (Laborer Characters)
entries.summary: A laborer character has the free Laborer Virtue and a Profession Ability instead of a Craft Ability, with that Profession also covering wage negotiations.
quotes: A laborer character must have the free Social Status Virtue Laborer.

entries.title: Covenant Craftsmen
entries.summary: Options for deciding how covenant craftsmen relate to guilds, from simply treating all of them as regular craftsmen to making them expelled, runaway or illegal guild members, and how trade-based covenants sell their goods.
quotes: The simplest method is to make every craftsman a regular craftsman.

entries.title: The Craft Ability (Defined by Vocation)
entries.summary: Rules clarification that a Craft Ability is normally named by the character's vocation rather than by the material worked, with a survey of the materials common crafts use.
quotes: a craftsman should define his Craft Abilities by vocation rather than material

entries.title: Craft Specialization
entries.summary: Guidance on choosing a Craft specialization: a single item, workshop activity or quality of goods, giving a bonus to that narrow aspect of the Ability.
quotes: The intent of the specialization rules is to allow a character to gain a +1 bonus to a single aspect of a broader Ability.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Traders (Social Status choices)
entries.summary: Every trader takes a Social Status Virtue matching the style of trade, in order of wealth: Merchant, Merchant Adventurer, Factor and Capo, adjusted by Wealthy or Poor; lists other Virtues and Flaws that suit merchant characters.
quotes: All traders have a Social Status Virtue representing the style of trade in which they engage.
These Virtues, in ascending order of wealth, are: Merchant (which suits urban merchants and local carriers), Merchant Adventurer, Factor, and Capo.

entries.title: Career Training Packages
entries.summary: A catalogue of trade and profession packages, each giving experience points in the key Abilities for a five-year or three-year option; some are marked Academic, Arcane or Martial and need a Virtue permitting those Abilities.
quotes: Five Years: +15 Athletics, +20 Brawl, +40 Single Weapon
Three Years: +5 Athletics, +10 Brawl, +30 Single Weapon

entries.title: Non-Career Training Packages
entries.summary: Three-year packages for background skills acquired through life rather than a trade (athlete, brawler, covenfolk, leader, rider and others), usually taken only once or twice.
quotes: Three Years: +15 Athletics, +30 Brawl
Three Years: +10 Folk Ken, +5 Charm, +30 Leadership

entries.title: Craftsman Training Package
entries.summary: The craft apprenticeship package, with notes on how long an apprenticeship takes and which packages journeymen and masters add.
quotes: Five Years: +10 Bargain, +25 Craft: Type A, +15 Craft: Type B, +15 Organization Lore: Guild, +10 Folk Ken

entries.title: Student Training Package
entries.summary: Academic schooling packages with different variants for cathedral, monastic, parish, tutor or university study; parish school is limited to the three-year option.
quotes: THREE YEARS (PARISH SCHOOL): +15 Artes Liberales, +30 Latin

entries.title: Creating Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces the step-by-step method for building statistics for any mundane beast, for example a shapechanger's animal form.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Beasts are sorted into four categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts), which drive later steps.
quotes: There are four categories of beasts: Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 2: Characteristics
entries.summary: Beasts use Cunning instead of Intelligence, spend characteristic points only on the four physical Characteristics, then adjust Strength and Quickness for Size; mental Characteristics come from the beast's type.
quotes: Unlike human characters, animals only spend points on their four physical characteristics (Stamina, Strength, Dexterity and Quickness).
Add twice the Size to Strength
Subtract Size from Quickness

entries.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication for each beast type.

versions.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication by beast type, and how Increased Characteristics applies to beasts.

entries.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of typical Size and physical Characteristics for common kinds of animal, as starting points for new beasts.

versions.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of sample physical Characteristics for common creature types, with the rule for applying Size adjustments after spending points.
quotes: add twice the Size to Strength and subtract the Size from Quickness

entries.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
entries.summary: How to scale a creature larger or smaller than average, such as after a Muto Animal spell, by adjusting Strength, Quickness and wound ranges per Size point.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense totals), and decrease the damage range for each wound level by 1 (minimum of 1)

versions.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
versions.summary: How to adjust Strength, Quickness and wound ranges for creatures bigger or smaller than their type's norm, including the effect of Muto Animal size spells.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage Total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense Totals)

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 3: Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Species Virtues and Flaws come free to all members of a species and are not balanced for game purposes, while exceptional individuals need balanced individual Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: It is recommended that a species have at least one point of Flaws for every three points of Virtues.

entries.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts
entries.summary: Lists Virtues and Flaws appropriate to beasts and a note that Improved Characteristics grants more characteristic points to larger creatures.
quotes: A creature of Size +1 or smaller gets 3 characteristic points from this Virtue as normal, a creature of Size +2 gets 6 characteristic points, a creature of size +3 gets 9 characteristic points, and so on.

alsoIn.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 4: Basic Abilities
entries.summary: Table of the Abilities every creature of each type has, plus rules that animals with Cunning cannot gain experience or learn new Abilities as adults except through an Animal Handling teacher.
quotes: Animals (at least, those with Cunning rather than Intelligence) cannot acquire experience points to improve their Abilities once they have reached adulthood, nor can they learn new Abilities.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 6: Combat Statistics
entries.summary: A beast's combat totals are calculated as normal using the Natural Weapons Table.
quotes: Combat Statistics are calculated as normal (page 393), using the Natural Weapons Table.

entries.title: Natural Weapons Table
entries.summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers for natural weapons such as teeth, claws, horns and hooves.
quotes: All natural weapons use the Brawl Ability.

entries.title: Appendix: Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces a step-by-step system for generating statistics for heartbeasts, familiars and other mundane creatures.

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Defines the four beast categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts, Clawed Beasts) and how Size steps relate to weight, with the bird adjustment.
quotes: A 1-point difference in Size doubles the weight

entries.title: Size Examples (animals)
entries.summary: Table of example animals at each Size value from -15 to +9.

entries.title: Ferocity (beast Virtue)
entries.summary: A beast-only Minor Virtue giving confidence points that can be used only in situations that trigger the animal's natural ferocity.
quotes: take 3 confidence Points and a confidence Score of 1

entries.title: Animal Creation Example: Bear
entries.summary: Worked example of the mundane beast design procedure, building a bear step by step and ending with a full stat block.

entries.title: Beast Statistics
entries.summary: Rules for mundane beast statistics: Characteristics outside the human range need no Virtue, Cunning replaces Intelligence, beasts cannot learn new Abilities without training, and they have no Might or vis.
quotes: Beasts do not need a Virtue or Flaw to have Characteristics outside the normal human range of –3 to +3.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 5: Qualities
entries.summary: Catalog of creature Qualities (such as Ambush Predator, Constriction, Grapple, Overrun, Swallow Whole, Tough Hide and Venomous) that adjust characteristics, Abilities, Protection and special attacks, with how extra Fatigue levels are granted.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level, two extra grant another Winded Level and another Weary Level, etc.

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 5: Qualities
entries.summary: A list of animal Qualities (Aggressive, Camouflage, Fast Runner, Grapple, Venomous and so on) that adjust Characteristics, grant Abilities or modify combat, plus how extra Fatigue levels are handled.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level
Add +3 to all rolls involving running.

entries.title: Angelic Powers
entries.summary: The powers every angel possesses: Angelic Mantle to take a material form, Enfolding to protect a soul or body from all harm briefly, and Envisioning to deliver Divine messages in dreams or waking visions.
quotes: All angels possess the following powers:
An angel may also Enfold a person's body (costing 10 Might points)

entries.title: Corrupt Beasts
entries.summary: How animals become corrupt (demonic influence, birth, Infernal auras or diabolists) and how to build one: start from a mundane beast, apply the compulsory Corrupted Beast Flaw and balance it with Virtues and Flaws from a restricted list.
quotes: To create the game statistics of a Corrupt Beast, start with the statistics of a mundane beast, and apply the Corrupted Beast Flaw.
The corpse of a corrupted beast typically contains one pawn of vis for each five points of Might it possessed.

entries.title: Virtues & Flaws for Corrupted Beasts
entries.summary: Lists the compulsory Flaw, the Virtues and the optional Flaws that a corrupted beast may be built from.
quotes: Optional Flaws: Horrifying Appearance, Demonic Weakness, Lesser Malediction

entries.title: Designing New Traditions
entries.summary: Guidance for building your own Infernal traditions out of Methods, Powers and other Favored Abilities, including how new Powers and Methods must be linked.
quotes: New Powers must be associated with at least one Method, and a new Method must be associated with at least two Powers.

entries.title: Fourth Edition Conversion: What Changed
entries.summary: A summary of the main rule changes from Fourth to Fifth Edition in character generation, covenants, magic, long-term events and combat, useful when updating old material or house rules.
quotes: Spell level is now subtracted from the casting total before determining Penetration.
Abilities now cost five times their (level + 1) to raise by one level.
First, Virtues and Flaws no longer have point values; they are split into Major and Minor.

entries.title: Fourth Edition Character Conversion
entries.summary: Rule-of-thumb steps for converting a Fourth Edition character: adjust age, keep Characteristics, convert Virtues and Flaws, rescale Ability experience, replace uncastable spells and turn Twilight Points into a Warping Score.
quotes: add 20% to a Fourth Edition character's age
Abilities: Leave at the old value, and multiply remaining XP by five.
Divide the number of Twilight Points by three, and use this as the Warping Score.

entries.title: The Limits of Education
entries.summary: Caps the starting score of Academic Abilities by the type of school attended, with major subjects at full limit and minor subjects at half (rounded up), and lists which subjects each institution teaches.
quotes: Attending any of these schools demands that the character have the Virtue: Educated.
Minor subjects are limited to half the regular score limit listed below, rounded up.

related.text: ArM5 p.31 Age limits on Abilities

entries.title: Town Officials as a Virtue
entries.requires: Optional rule: Town Magistrate Social Status Virtue
entries.summary: Advises treating town office as part of a story, but offers a variant of the Town Magistrate Virtue for a general town official, with the Civil and Canon Law requirement and Academic Abilities benefit dropped.
quotes: a Virtue modeled upon the Minor Social Status Virtue: Town Magistrate (see Crime) can be used

entries.title: Wealthy and Poor Characters (Training Packages)
