entries.summary: Adjusts the age gained from training packages for Wealthy characters (younger) and Poor characters (older).
quotes: reduce the character's post-childhood age by one quarter
increase the post-childhood age by one half

entries.title: Magician Training Package
entries.summary: A package for characters with Supernatural Abilities, which also lets the character sacrifice experience to buy Enriched Objects of Virtue.
quotes: Five Years: +15 Concentration, +30 Magic Lore, +30 Penetration

entries.title: Offices
entries.summary: Explains what an officer of a lord is, how officers differ from hereditary vassals, what their underlings will and will not do, and that characters built as officers need the Temporal Influence Virtue. The individual offices that follow are descriptive.
quotes: Characters designed as officers need the Temporal Influence Virtue.

entries.title: Squire
entries.requires: Gentleman, Knight or Landed Noble Virtue
entries.summary: Describes the squire as a young knight-in-training or as a landholder who has chosen not to take knighthood, and says which social Virtues such a character may take.
quotes: A squire may take the Gentleman, Knight, or Landed Noble Virtues.

entries.title: Bacheler Knight
entries.summary: The household knights of a lord's mesnie: which Virtues and Flaw they normally have, what their lord provides, and how rich bachelers can be Landed Nobles.
quotes: A bacheler knight has the Virtues Knight and Protection, and the Oath of Fealty Flaw or Free Choice.

entries.title: Knight Banneret
entries.summary: The rank of a knight who leads other knights under his own banner, how it is claimed or awarded, and the land and Virtues that go with it, which make it economically close to a Wealthy Landed Noble.
quotes: A knight may claim this rank simply by arriving at a battle with a force of ten knights all clad in his livery and willing to kill as instructed.
Bannerets are always Knights and are generally Landed Nobles.

entries.title: Oath of Fealty (Major Story Flaw)
entries.summary: Optional guidance on adapting the Oath of Fealty Flaw: allodial holders need not have one, and troupes may allow insignificant oaths that do not count as Flaws so knights can still take other Story Flaws.
quotes: A holder of allodial land need not have an Oath of Fealty.

entries.title: Knightly Demands (Major Story Flaw)
entries.requires: Optional rule replacing Oath of Fealty
entries.summary: A variant Major Story Flaw that lets the Storyguide pull any knight into plots typical of medieval ballads, suited to high fantasy, mobile sagas; it replaces Oath of Fealty entirely.
quotes: troupes may simply state that all knights have a Major Story Flaw, called Knightly Demands

entries.title: Landed Noble (Major Virtue)
entries.summary: Extended description of what the Landed Noble Virtue provides at Poor, standard and Wealthy levels: manors, knight service, levies, free seasons per year and spending money.
quotes: He has one season of free time per year.
This Virtue leaves the lord two seasons of free time per year, and ten pounds to spend on largesse, war, or other discretionary matters.
These lands provide the lord with the service of four knights, other than himself, 5 serjants, and 50 villeins.

entries.title: Great Noble (Two Major Virtues)
entries.summary: How the Great Noble Virtue is priced for characters of greater baron rank or higher, and a warning about integrating such characters into a covenant-focused saga.
quotes: Two Major Virtues for characters played in lieu of magi, as major protagonists in the plot.

entries.title: Baron
entries.requires: Virtue: Great Noble or Landed Noble
entries.summary: What it means to be a baron, the difference between greater and lesser barons, the Virtues and Flaw they usually take, military service owed and how much surplus money poor, average and Wealthy barons have.
quotes: A man is considered greater baron if he has at least some land held directly from the king and expenses of at least 400 pounds per year.
An average baron has a surplus of 40 pounds per year that may be spent as he wishes.

entries.title: Earl or Count
entries.summary: The resources of a count or earl: his Virtue, yearly expenditure, the force he is expected to bring to battle, and spending money for average and wealthy counts.
quotes: A count has a yearly expenditure of at least 1000 pounds.
The average count might be required to bring 50 knights to battle, along with their sergeants and 500 infantry.

entries.title: Count Palatine and Marcher Lord
entries.summary: Counts given extra powers on a difficult border, with the special rights of marcher lords and the note that they are effectively Wealthy counts with fewer knights and more infantry.
quotes: Some marcher lords are effectively Wealthy counts.

entries.title: Duke
entries.summary: The standing of a duke or duchess, the Virtue they take and a rough estimate of a duke's personal forces and spending.
quotes: As a rough estimate, a duke has, at minimum, personal forces that include 75 knights, their sergeants, and 750 infantry.

entries.title: King
entries.summary: Defines kingship and succession, and in sidebars gives the scale of a king's lands, income, household army and greater barons, how few families make up the ruling class, and the effects of anointing, including minor magic resistance.
quotes: A king is technically a Great Noble and need not be a Knight, although virtually all are.
All kings have minor magic resistance as noted in Chapter Four: Interference.

related.text: Magic Resistance For Church Officers and Sovereigns

entries.title: Caballero
entries.summary: The requirements and legal protection of a caballero's rank in Iberia, and how to build one as a player character using the Knight Virtue or covenant gear, with local custom usable as a Major Story Flaw.
quotes: Players designing caballeros can either take the Knight Minor Social Status Virtue, or just use gear that belongs to the covenant.

entries.title: Caballero Villano
entries.requires: Wealthy Knight tied to a town
entries.summary: A town-bound mounted warrior who keeps tax exemptions by residing in town and mustering for its defense; tied by his Dependents rather than honor, though troupes may allow Knightly Duties instead.
quotes: This style of Wealthy Knight is tied to the town by his Dependents rather than his honor, although troupes may permit players to select Knightly Duties instead.

entries.title: Caballero Hidalgo (or Fidalgo)
entries.requires: Virtue: Knight and Gentleman or Landed Noble
entries.summary: An ancestral caballero from a family that supports him in matters of honor, comparable to an English lord of the manor, with the Virtues he normally has.
quotes: Hidalgos have the Knight Virtue and either Gentleman or Landed Noble.

entries.title: Ricohombre
entries.summary: The Iberian aristocratic upper class: how their honores work, the military service and restrictions they have, and the Great Noble Virtue they take.
quotes: They have the Great Noble Virtue.

entries.title: Paid Rights: A Free Virtue
entries.requires: Female character who has paid a fine for a normally forbidden right
entries.summary: Lets a woman character who paid a large fine or fee before play to hold a right normally forbidden to women take a free Virtue called Paid Rights, optionally balanced by a Story Flaw. It cannot buy anything that only men may do in Church administration, and knighthood is difficult.
quotes: She may choose a free Virtue, called Paid Rights, to note that she has paid for the right to do a certain thing that is generally forbidden for women.

entries.title: Castle Free Choices
entries.requires: Virtue: Landed Noble or Great Noble
entries.summary: Lists the simple strongholds (island, manor house, ringwork, small tower) a Landed or Great Noble can pick for free, with a description of how each works defensively.
quotes: may select any of these options to describe his stronghold without spending extra money annually

entries.title: Minor Castles
entries.requires: Virtue: Landed Noble or Great Noble
entries.summary: Describes the shell keep and tower keep castle options for Landed or Great Nobles, with the yearly upkeep paid out of the character's frivolous spending money and the cost of extra guards.
quotes: must pay two pounds per year
at the rate of one pound per man per year for mediocre servants

entries.title: Curtain Walls and Mural Towers
entries.summary: Describes great castles with curtain walls and mural towers, their yearly maintenance cost, the extra infantry required as guards, and the political cost of building many towers.
quotes: A castle costs five pounds a year to maintain

entries.title: Keep Alternatives for Castles with Curtain Walls
entries.summary: Options for the keep of a curtain-walled castle (hall keep, courtyard castle, gatehouse keep) plus what a barbican and moat represent in game terms and how they affect upkeep.
quotes: A barbican and moat are included in the cost of a castle with curtain walls.
A moat has no upkeep fee; it's a free choice for characters with castles that have curtain walls.

entries.title: Sign Language (Monastery)
entries.summary: A language Ability specific to a monastery or nunnery, with a fluency scale and defaults to the sign languages of related and unrelated houses at different penalties.
quotes: It defaults to an Ability in the language of other monasteries of the same order at –3

entries.title: Characters in a Nunnery
entries.requires: Playing a nun or other woman of a nunnery
entries.summary: Advice on building nun characters: which Flaws, Virtues and Abilities fit, plus background types (the Scholar, the Refugee, the Prisoner, the Revolutionary) and which Virtues and Flaws explain why a woman ends up in a nunnery.
quotes: Most nuns come from a noble family, so Privileged Upbringing is a common Virtue.
Artes Liberales, Latin, and Church Lore are the Abilities expected of all nun characters, even if only at a low level

related.text: Chapter 4: The Rule and Religious Life

entries.title: Templar Brother-Knights
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-knight
entries.summary: Entry requirements, expected prior combat experience, group training and restrictions on possessions for Templar brother-knights, who are the core rank of the order.
quotes: By 1220, the Templars require a brother-knight to be of noble birth, the son of a secular knight, or the son of the daughter of a knight to be admitted to this rank.

entries.title: Templar Brother-Sergeants
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-sergeant
entries.summary: The commoner rank of the Templars, serving as foot soldiers and as administrators, artisans and craftsmen under the same rule as the brother-knights.
quotes: Brother-sergeants are from common backgrounds and social statuses, and are recruited from a wider area.

entries.title: Templar Brother-Priests
entries.requires: Joining the Knights Templar as a brother-priest
entries.summary: How priests join the Templars and the sacramental authority they hold within the order, which exceeds that of local clergy.
quotes: They can give services, celebrate Mass, hear confessions, give absolution for most offenses (except grievous sins such as murder, simony, or heresy) and bury the dead.

entries.title: Templar Confreres and Consoeurs
entries.requires: Associate membership in the Knights Templar
entries.summary: Lay associate members of the Templars, who take vows without full profession and may keep their own homes, including temporary-vow pilgrims and wives of Templars.
quotes: Confreres and consoeurs cannot vote in chapter meetings but otherwise interact daily with full members

entries.title: Joining the Templars: The Membership Ritual
entries.summary: Step-by-step account of the traditional ceremony in which an applicant is questioned, tested with a menial task if a commoner, swears his vows and is invested with the mantle.
quotes: Then he then swears the vows of obedience, chastity, and poverty, and promises to conquer and defend Jerusalem.

entries.title: Playing a Templar Character
entries.summary: Three ways to make a Templar playable despite the strictness of the rule: loose discipline (with a Story Flaw if the rule is to matter), outside responsibilities, or a lone Templar at a remote outpost.
quotes: Templar characters should take an appropriate Story Flaw if they want to play through stories involving the rule and Templar restrictions.

entries.title: Templars and the Wealthy Virtue
entries.summary: Templars may take the Wealthy Virtue or Poor Flaw, but these represent responsibilities, authority and free time within a regimented day instead of personal money.
quotes: Templar characters can take the Wealthy Major Virtue, and also the Poor Major Flaw.

entries.title: Creating Templar Characters
entries.requires: Templar membership (Brother-Knight, Brother-Priest, Brother-Sergeant or other Templar Virtue)
entries.summary: Explains how Templar characters are built, with Templar-specific Social Status Virtues that set which Ability groups may be taken at creation, who the character answers to, and starting Reputation. Includes the Templar Prestige and associate/servant options.
quotes: You may take Academic and Martial Abilities during character generation.
He starts with a Reputation of level 4 within the Templars.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.92

entries.title: Templar Equipment
entries.summary: Lists the standard issue arms, armor, clothing, horses and squires for Templar brother-knights and brother-sergeants, and how squires differ from chivalric squires.
quotes: Each brother-knight is issued with three horses and a squire

entries.title: Organization Lore: Knights Templar
entries.requires: Virtue granting Templar membership (or troupe permission)
entries.summary: A new General Lore Ability covering Templar rules, personalities, provinces, tactics, sign language and ciphers. Normally only available to characters who belong to the order.
quotes: This Ability also gives the character knowledge of the Templar sign language
Specialties: personalities, history, politics, tactics, sign language, a particular region. (General)

entries.title: Joining the Franciscans
entries.requires: Franciscan friar or Poor Sister character
entries.summary: Explains how to build male and female Franciscan characters: the Mendicant Friar Virtue for men, and the Religious Social Status plus suitable Virtues and Flaws for women. Notes that the usual Monastic Vows requirement can be swapped for alternatives.
quotes: While the Virtue Mendicant Friar covers male Franciscan characters, it is not appropriate for female Franciscan characters.

related.text: Chapter 3: The Diocese, Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: The Dominicans (character guidance)
entries.summary: Describes the Order of Preachers and advises that a Dominican character takes the Educated Virtue and, if male without a university degree, is usually sent to study theology and ordained.
quotes: A character wishing to be a member of the Order of Preachers will have the Educated Virtue

entries.title: Potent Magic
entries.summary: Reproduces the Potent Magic Hermetic Virtue, which gives a bonus in a narrow field like a Magical Focus and lets the magus design Potent spells. Several mysteries in this book rely on it.
quotes: grants a +3 bonus to Lab Totals and Casting Scores
grants a +6 bonus to Lab Totals and Casting Scores

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus table

entries.title: Designing Covenant Libraries
entries.summary: At covenant creation, Potency counts toward a Potent spell's level when spending Build Points on Lab Texts.
quotes: add Potency (if any) to spell level when counting Build Points

entries.title: Astrological Magical Focus and Potent Magic
entries.requires: Virtue: Magical Focus or Potent Magic (astrological)
entries.summary: Allows a Magical Focus or Potent Magic to be defined by a single astrological sign, planet or house; spells that use such a benefit count as Astrological spells.
quotes: Any magus may have a Major Magical Focus or Major Potent Magic covering effects governed by a single astrological sign.

entries.title: (Astrological) Mutable Virtue or Flaw
entries.summary: Lets a Virtue or Flaw apply only in the four mutable signs: Major ones drop to Minor, Minor ones are doubled in intensity.
quotes: the Virtue or Flaw is reduced to being Minor
the effect is doubled in intensity

entries.title: Story Hook: The Language of Innocence
entries.summary: Option for a Gifted child raised without language influences to begin with a limited, undevelopable score in Dead Language (Adamic) that can be taught on to others.
quotes: may begin with a score of 2 in Dead Language (Adamic)

entries.title: Mechanica of Heron: awakened simulacra (anima)
entries.summary: Rules for building a simulacrum of an animal, working out its Magic Might from size and material, awakening its anima with a cumulative-bonus lab project, and playing the resulting sentient mechanica (traits, Abilities, powers of movement and speech).
quotes: Anima's Magic Might: Size + Material Base Points + (lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales)
Awaken Anima Total: Intelligence + Mechanica of Heron Ability + (lower of Philosophiae or Artes Liberales) + Aura
Awaken Anima Level: 9 + Magnitude of Anima's Magic Might

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.129 automata powers

entries.title: False Power (Flaw)
entries.summary: Extended rules for a Supernatural Virtue that is also tainted by the Infernal, including how it reads to investigation, optional treatment as an Infernal Power, repentance, and taking the Flaw several times.
quotes: using the Infernal Power column of the realm interaction chart

entries.title: False Gift (False Magic)
entries.requires: Virtue: False Gift; Flaw: False Power
entries.summary: Explains the Infernally corrupted Gift: it carries the usual social penalties, its Supernatural Abilities are False Powers, Warping causes Vituperation instead of Twilight, and confessing and being absolved removes the Gift.
quotes: When exposed to Warping, instead of experiencing Twilight, a character with the False Gift must undergo Vituperation.
The False Gift has no cost, like its magical counterpart, though it requires the False Power Flaw

entries.title: Options for Characters Retrieved From Purgatory
entries.summary: Lists the existing Virtues, Flaws and character templates that suit characters who have been rescued from Purgatory or brought back from the dead.
quotes: Raised From The Dead (Major Story/ Supernatural Flaw, Realms of Power: the Divine, page 36)

related.text: Realms of Power: the Divine p.36 Raised From The Dead
Realms of Power: Magic pp.96-97 Drowned Men
Realms of Power: Magic pp.115-118 Ghosts

entries.title: New Virtue: Folk Magic
entries.summary: A new Minor Supernatural Virtue giving very minor spell-like magic in one narrow area, keyed to a Realm Lore. It explains the allowed categories of effect, the casting cost and preparation, and the halved Casting Total formula.
quotes: Your Casting Total is equal to (Stamina + (Realm) Lore + Aura modifier + stress die) / 2.
To cast a spell you must expend a fatigue level, whether the spell succeeds or fails.

entries.title: Teutonic Knight Characters
entries.summary: Character-creation guidance for Teutonic Order members (priests, knights, graymantles): typical Poor Flaw and relic Virtue choices, favored Abilities, and new Minor Social Status Virtues that set which Abilities may be taken at creation.
quotes: Teutonic Knights very commonly carry relics (the Relic Virtue), often in the hilt of their swords.
so knowledge of Dominion Lore is highly prized

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.41

entries.title: Scholomance Schooling (pupils and curriculum)
entries.summary: Explains who is admitted to the Scholomance, what pupils are taught, what they must produce, and which background Virtues attendance can justify for companions, Redcaps and apprentices.
quotes: It accepts ten pupils at a time, all at once, and they remain for a total of seven years.
Pupils are required to make copies of some of the texts that they study at the school, and to write at least one summa or three tractatus during their stay.
Attending the Scholomance is a good way to explain Virtues such as Educated, Arcane Lore, Privileged Upbringing or (for apprentices) Skilled Parens.

entries.title: Creating a Vampire Character
entries.summary: States that vampires are storyguide characters, with only a narrow exception for self-aware kukudhi vampires as possible player characters in a high-power saga.
quotes: Vampires are intended as storyguide characters.

entries.title: Vampiric Virtues, Flaws, and Powers
entries.summary: Lists the Virtues and Flaws every vampire must have when built as a faerie character: a physical form, a cognizance level, a social-interaction trait, Feast of the Dead, a Traditional Ward of sunlight, and the Sap the Life Lesser Power.
quotes: All vampires have the Feast of the Dead Virtue that allows them to obtain vitality from human life, and have a Traditional Ward of sunlight which causes them to take damage if exposed to the light of day.
Finally, all vampires have the Sap the Life Lesser Power (see insert).

entries.title: Common Vampire Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Short lists of Virtues and Flaws commonly given to vampires when designing them as faerie characters.

entries.title: Powers for Vampires (sidebar)
entries.summary: Sidebar of ready-made faerie powers for vampires, grouped as Lesser Powers, Focus Powers and Personal Powers, each with Might cost, Initiative and Hermetic-style parameters.

entries.title: Lesser Powers and Converting to Greater Powers
entries.summary: Explains that each Lesser Power Virtue buys a set number of power levels and gives the conversion to a Greater Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative penalty.
quotes: Each Lesser Power Virtue is a Minor Virtue that grants 25 levels of powers.
halve the Might cost and the penalty to Initiative

entries.title: Ways to Kill a Vampire
entries.summary: Explains that the correct folk rituals sate a vampire for good, after which the faerie reforms elsewhere, whereas a botched killing lets it return within days or weeks. Lists methods of dispatch of which one is picked for each vampire.
quotes: For each vampire, pick a method of dispatch that results in permanent death:

entries.title: The Varcolac and Vukodlak (werewolf living vampires)
entries.summary: Describes werewolf-like varcolaci, how they come about, their wolf brotherhoods that hunt vampires and the mischievous ones that are Nightwalkers. Says which Virtue a varcolac character takes and that they die as bestial vampires.
quotes: A varcolac character has either the Shapeshifter Virtue if he was born a werewolf, or the Skinchanger Virtue if he has learned to change shape.

entries.title: Heart of the Storm Initiation
entries.requires: Initiation: Heart of the Storm (Storm Wizards)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the initiation ease factor, initiation total formula and script bonus for the storm wizard initiation that grants Giant Blood.
quotes: Initiation Ease Factor: 21
Presence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizards + Script Bonus

entries.title: The Sabotnik (Saturday-born hunters)
entries.requires: Born on a Saturday or during the Unclean Days or Wolf Holiday
entries.summary: Describes the sabotnik, who is born on a Saturday and so is immune to the direct powers of vampires bound by that taboo, can sense vampires and magicians, and may be fated to become a vampire. Notes the option to randomly determine birth days.
quotes: Anyone born on a Saturday is therefore immune to the direct powers of such vampire.

entries.title: The Glog (vampire-protecting hunters)
entries.requires: Born feet first, with teeth or with red hair
entries.summary: Describes the glog, a hunter specialising in protecting people from vampires, who crafts defensive weapons from black hawthorn and is usually aggressive and physically gifted.

entries.title: The Vampirdzhi (son of a vampire)
entries.summary: Describes vampirdzhia, sons of vampires who become hunters out of necessity rather than tradition, may be trained, and also risk rising as vampires after death.
quotes: Only men are believed to be vampirdzhia; the daughters of vampires become witches instead.

entries.title: Hunter Characters
entries.summary: Character-creation guidance for sabotnici, glogove, kresnici, taltós, dhampiri and vampirdzhia: suggested Virtues, Flaws, Arts and Abilities, and a note that the Gift is not required.
quotes: Sabotnici and glogove characters should have the Second Sight Virtue, and possibly the Magic Sensitivity Virtue in addition.
Dhampir and vampirdzhi characters should take the Dhampir Virtue (see earlier) to represent their vampire ancestry.

entries.title: The Oak Gild (Eichengilde)
entries.summary: The largest and oldest Rhine gild, devoted to tradition, respect for the Founders and elders, and shunning outside wisdom, and led by the Prima of Bonisagus.

entries.title: The Hawthorn Gild (Weissdorngilde)
entries.summary: The smallest and one of the oldest Rhine gilds, which seeks to protect wild places and creatures from mundanes and is dominated by Bjornaer Wilderists.

entries.title: The Ash Gild (Eschengilde)
entries.summary: An aggressive, magically powerful gild favoring dominion over the magi's lands and open dealing with mundanes, with a hidden focus on combating the Order of Odin.

entries.title: The Elder Gild (Holundergilde)
entries.summary: A gild, largely of Merinita magi, devoted to preserving the fae and promoting friendly contact between magi and faeries.

entries.title: The Linden Gild (Lindengilde)
entries.summary: A small, altruistic go-between gild founded after the Schism War to build trust and peaceful resolution between magi and covenants.

entries.title: The Apple Gild (Apfelgilde)
entries.summary: The newest and weakest Rhine gild, advocating peaceful relations with and acceptance in the mundane world.

entries.title: Pomeranian werewolves (skinchanger families)
entries.requires: Born into a Pomeranian werewolf family (storyguide approval)
entries.summary: Explains how shapeshifting is inherited in Pomeranian werewolf families, which Virtue or Flaw a child receives, how animals react to them, and offers a list of suitable additional Virtues and Flaws for playing a werewolf companion.
quotes: A child born into a werewolf family will acquire the Skinchanger Virtue.
Those unlucky enough to be born into human families will usually acquire the Lycanthrope Flaw, and be unable to control their change.

entries.title: Radegast
entries.summary: Describes the pagan Slavic god Radegast and the Virtues and Flaw his favored followers tend to display, useful when building his devotees as characters.
quotes: Those he favors often display the Inspirational and Great Presence Virtues, as well as the Overconfident Flaw.

related.text: Between the Devil and the Deep Blue Sea (Chapter 11)

entries.title: The Blood of Merovech
entries.requires: Merovingian descent (Supernatural Virtue such as Greater Immunity: Drowning; Royal Touch)
entries.summary: Sidebar on the Merovingian bloodline: which Supernatural Virtues descendants of Merovech commonly carry, the red-cross birthmark, and theories on the origin of the king's Royal Touch.
quotes: most of the descendants of Merovech have a Supernatural Virtue
Greater Immunity: Drowning

related.text: Chapter 10: Normandy Sagas, The Tradition of Kings

entries.title: The Carolingian Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar noting that characters of Carolingian descent may be politically important and often carry a particular Virtue.
quotes: Those of Carolingian blood often have the Virtue Mythic Presence.

entries.title: The Capetian Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar on the pious Capetian bloodline, some of whose members manifest a faith-related Virtue.
quotes: Some members of the bloodline manifest this as the Virtue True Faith

entries.title: The Angevin Blood
entries.summary: Sidebar on the legend of Melusine and the uncertain, unpredictable supernatural heritage of the Angevin line, left for the troupe to define.
quotes: This tainted blood runs in the Angevin veins till this day, and may manifest in unpredictable ways.

entries.title: Luctationes
entries.summary: Tribunal-owned vis sources that need skill or risk to harvest are open contests for any magus each year, confer no lasting rights, and cost no Build Points unless a covenant has exclusive access.
quotes: If a covenant does have exclusive access to a luctatio for some reason, then it is costed as a vis source with the Contested Resource Hook.

entries.title: Eremites and Coenobites
entries.summary: Solitary magi (eremites) and communities that fail the vis requirement (coenobia) cannot hold seisins and must rely on Tourney tropaea and luctationes, competing as individuals.
quotes: An eremite is forbidden by the Peripheral Code from owning a seisin, and he must rely upon tropaeum leases won at the Tourney or attending luctatio for his vis supply.

entries.title: The Dynatoi as Player Characters
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Suggests Virtues and Flaws that fit a character from the dispossessed Byzantine nobility.
quotes: Such a character is likely to have the Privileged Upbringing Virtue to represent his former status.

entries.title: Languages of the Theban Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Lists the regional languages and dialect specialties, says Romaic and Classical Greek are separate Abilities, and gives a table of comprehension penalties between related languages.
quotes: Romaic Greek and Classical Greek are mutually intelligible, but they are separate Abilities.
Romaic Greek vs Classical Greek|-2
* Penalty applies to both speakers.

entries.title: The Alaphroiskiotoi
entries.summary: Folklore holds that those born on a Saturday have a light shadow, usually represented by Second Sight, Dowsing or Magic Sensitivity, and special power over vrykolakes.
quotes: Most alaphroiskiotoi have the Second Sight Virtue, although others possess Dowsing or Magic Sensitivity instead

entries.title: Lesbos: reversed gender roles and character creation
entries.summary: Natives of Lesbos live in a society where women hold higher status than men, so characters who have not adjusted to other regions' gender roles are advised to take the Social Handicap Flaw, and certain Virtues are very common.
quotes: should take the Social Handicap Flaw
The Enchanting Music and Free Expression Virtues are very common.

entries.title: Porphyrogenitos: supernatural Virtue table for characters born in the purple
entries.requires: Character born in the Porphyry Chamber, Constantinople
entries.summary: A character born in the Porphyry Chamber gains a free Minor Supernatural Virtue whose realm is determined by a die roll, with a small chance of a Major Virtue instead.
quotes: If a character is born in the chamber, the storyguide should roll a simple die and consult the following:

entries.title: Channeling a Greek god (Elysian Ecstasy and Olympian Pact)
entries.requires: Initiation: Elysian Ecstasy (Minor) or Olympian Pact (Major)
entries.summary: Rules for the roll to channel a Greek god, with a table of Ease Factors giving Personality Trait bonuses, Sympathy Trait points and (for Olympian Pact) access to the god's powers, plus the preparation hours, failure cost and duration.
quotes: Channeling a Greek God: (Characteristic) + Faerie Lore + stress die + aura
A character may spend additional hours in this frenetic state, with each additional hour adding +1 to his die roll.
A character gains Sympathy Traits, Personality Traits, and powers (for Olympian Pact) for a number of hours equal to the total rolled.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie, pages 102-105 (Sympathy Traits)
Realms of Power: Magic, page 88 (Spiritual Pact)

entries.title: Blood of the Old Gods and Sympathy Traits
entries.requires: Virtue: Blood of the Old Gods (Minor or Major Supernatural)
entries.summary: A variety of Faerie Blood that grants a Sympathy Trait which can replace an Ability speciality on applicable rolls (always as a stress roll), is raised with experience, and is capped by the Warping Score.
quotes: A Sympathy Trait can replace the character's speciality on any applicable Ability roll, but doing so always makes the roll a stress roll.

entries.title: The Akh (Egyptian Daimon)
entries.summary: Explains how the ba, ka and khu fuse into an akh, a Daimon, and how to build one as a Magic Spirit with a Magic Might range, as a Winter creature summoned by name or relics.
quotes: Assume a Magic Might Score of 20 for noblemen who have the simplest coffin texts, up to 60 for the greatest pharaohs

entries.title: Slavery in a Saga (slave, owner and slaver characters)
entries.requires: Saga set in Egypt or Nubia (Slavelands)
entries.summary: Guidance for troupes on playing slaves, free Aithiopians, slave owners, slavers and campaigners against slavery, including which Virtues and Flaws suit each character type.
quotes: Characters who are slavers should take the Merchant Social Status Virtue if they are mostly involved in the transport of slaves, or the Mercenary Captain Social Status Virtue if they are captors.

entries.title: A Free Aithiopian Character
entries.requires: Aithiopian character in a saga set outside the Slavelands
entries.summary: Says which Social Status Flaw a free Aithiopian character should take and suggests related Story Flaws.
quotes: Free Aithiopians should take either the Outsider or Outcast Social Status Flaw in any saga set outside of the Slavelands.

entries.title: A Slave Owner Character
entries.requires: Saga set in Egypt or Nubia
entries.summary: In Egypt and Nubia owning slaves needs no Virtue, and a Christian owner in a Christian kingdom takes a small Local Reputation for the social disapproval.
quotes: A Christian slave owner in a Christian kingdom has a Local Reputation at a score of 1, representing the social disapproval that this practice engenders.

entries.title: The Dihi (detachable-head race)
entries.requires: Dihi heritage (Blemmya and human offspring from northern Atbai)
entries.summary: Rules for playing a Dihi, whose head detaches under shock or strain: the stress-die trigger, botch effects, reattaching the head, inheritance, and the Flaw and Virtue that suit the condition.
quotes: Under situations of physical or emotional stress roll a stress die; if the result is 9 or more then her head detaches.
It takes a round to reattach the head to the body.

entries.title: Kassalan Exorcists
entries.requires: Training by the Mortuary Society of Kassala
entries.summary: Describes the typical Virtues, Abilities and tactics of an exorcist of the Mortuary Society, who specialises in laying ghosts and the walking dead.
quotes: Exorcists tend to concentrate on low level, high Penetration effects, and often work in concert to destroy powerful ghosts.

entries.title: New Virtue: Kassalan Exorcism
entries.summary: A limited supernatural casting method for wards against ghosts and the walking dead and for stripping their Might, with its own fatigue cost, preparation time, Casting Total and Penetration rules.
quotes: To cast a spell you must expend a Fatigue level, whether the spell succeeds or fails.
Your Casting Total is equal to (Stamina + Organization Lore: Mortuary Society + Aura modifier + stress die) / 2.

entries.title: The Alchemists of Soba
entries.requires: Virtue: Soban Alchemy or Alchemist of Soba
entries.summary: Explains how to build a Soban Alchemist character, the Abilities and patronage they need, the obligation to stay near Soba, and how the craft is taught from books or by initiation.
quotes: They also require the Profession: Apothecary Ability to manage and run a well-stocked alchemist's laboratory.

entries.title: Mythic Aithiopians as characters
entries.summary: Explains how to build a Mythic Aithiopian character: they carry an Outsider status in Nubia and gain tribe-specific intrinsic Virtues and Flaws on top of the normal allotment, or may be built as Magic Humans instead.
quotes: Aithiopes have intrinsic Virtues and Flaws, which are in addition to the normal allotment for characters.
They automatically receive the effects of the Outsider Social Status Flaw within Nubia
Magic Humans are by default immune to aging and deprivation

entries.title: Rhizophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the root-eating Rhizophagi, expert herbalists and poisoners, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw and a short explanation of the Herbalism Ability.
quotes: the Herbalism Virtue grants access to a special Ability called Herbalism

entries.title: Icthyophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the coastal fish-eating Icthyophagi, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw and the properties of their preserved fish bricks as travel food.
quotes: A month's worth of this food weighs just one point of Load.

entries.title: Hylophagus characters
entries.summary: Describes the tree-dwelling Hylophagi as intelligent monkeys built from baboon statistics plus extra Virtues and Flaws, and suggests using their village-trees as covenant sites and the Hylophagi as covenfolk.
quotes: Use the statistics for baboons in the Bestiary, but add the Perfect Balance Virtue and the Primitive Equipment Flaw
A village tree has the approximate interior dimensions of a Mystic Tower.

related.text: ArM5 p.139 Free the Striding Tree

entries.title: Cynegus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the hunters of the Cynegi, who use kombe-laced arrows; gives the Stamina roll against the poison, the Profession: Prepare Kombe Ability and its application roll, and the tribe's intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: must make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 12
characters should roll Dexterity + Profession: Prepare Kombè against an Ease Factor of (usually) 6

entries.title: Struthophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the ostrich-riding Struthophagi, valued as light cavalry, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: Puissant Ride; Small Frame

entries.title: Acridophagus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the locust-eating Acridophagi, whose intrinsic Flaw is a curse that makes Aging rolls start early when the louse infestation begins.
quotes: The Acridophagus curse causes them to start making Aging rolls at 15

entries.title: Cynamolgus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the dog-pack herders of the Cynamolgi, who may use Animal Handling in place of Leadership when commanding their dogs, with their intrinsic Virtue and Flaw.
quotes: a Cynamolgus can act as the leader of a trained group of dogs, using his Animal Handling in place of Leadership

entries.title: Megabarus characters
entries.summary: Character notes for the Megabari herders, giving separate intrinsic Virtues and Flaws for men and for women.
quotes: Puissant Bows; Prohibition (harming women)

entries.title: Spell Mastery Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Spell Mastery Abilities belong to magi and concern casting Formulaic and Ritual spells; full rules are in the Hermetic Magic chapter.
quotes: Spell Mastery Abilities can only be taken by magi

entries.title: Bjornaer: The Heartbeast
entries.requires: House Bjornaer: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery
entries.summary: Bjornaer magi take the form of one mundane creature using the Heartbeast Ability; the form cannot be changed by Hermetic magic, they can cast in beast form at a penalty, cannot bind familiars, and gain little Warping from changing.
quotes: In that case, a roll of Stamina + Heartbeast against an Ease Factor set by the storyguide allows the character to change anyway.
As a rule of thumb, 3 + the magnitude of the transforming magic is a reasonable number.

entries.title: Secret Name (Minor House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer (Clan Ilfetu): Initiation of Secret Name
entries.summary: A minor House mystery that severs the sympathetic resonances of a magus's name: old Arcane Connections expire and Sympathetic Connections never work against him, though anyone who knows the secret name ignores spell level in Penetration.
quotes: All Arcane Connections to the magus which date from before the ritual immediately expire upon its completion, and all Sympathetic Connections become invalid.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition Synthemata Magic

entries.title: Clan Arelie (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Remember clan, its political stance and roles, and lists its three Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Tree, the Deed of Forgotten Lore and the Oath of the Empty Hand) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The initiate is hanged by his wrists for four days

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 3: Curious Common Magics (Art of Memory)

entries.title: Clan Ilfetu (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Teach clan, the only one that initiates the House Mysteries, and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial and Oath of the Prophet and the Deed of Honor) with the Virtues and Flaws gained.
quotes: To be a member of this clan, you must take the Clan Ilfetu Minor Virtue.
The Initiate is pinned under a large rock for 9 days and acquires the Visions Flaw

entries.title: Clan Maruhs (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Strive clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Chains, the Deed of Emulation and the Oath of the Muse) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: Bound by magical chains and cast into a pit

entries.title: Clan Midusulf (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Lead clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of the Sacred Marriage, the Deed of Glory and the Oath of Steadfastness) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate is ritually wedded to the earth through the letting of blood

entries.title: Clan Sirnas (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Protect clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self Control, the Deed of the Woodland Warden and the Oath of the Helpful Stranger) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must starve himself until he collapses

entries.title: Clan Wilkis (Bjornaer clan and initiations)
entries.summary: Describes the Nourish clan and lists its Clan Initiations (the Trial of Self-Negation, the Deed of Fealty and the Oath of Completion) with the Virtues and Flaws each grants.
quotes: The Initiate must perform humiliating and degrading acts before many witnesses

entries.title: The Heartbeast (concept and Ritual of Twelve Years)
entries.requires: Virtue: Heartbeast (Ritual of Twelve Years, House Bjornaer)
entries.summary: Explains what the heartbeast is, that only the Ritual of Twelve Years grants the Heartbeast Virtue and Ability, and how it differs from magical shapechanging (a true animal, not a disguise). Also covers pregnancy, cross-species children and the House's bond of kinship.
quotes: Undergoing the Ritual of Twelve Years is the only way to gain the Heartbeast Virtue (and Ability)

related.text: ArM5 pp.91-92 Outer Mystery of House Bjornaer

entries.title: Choosing the Heartbeast
entries.summary: Advice for players on choosing a heartbeast that fits the character: expect physical signs, think about other Bjornaer in the troupe, and remember a magus can have only one.
quotes: Naturally, a magus can only have one heartbeast, for he only has a single spirit.

entries.title: Heartbeast Temperaments and Restrictions
entries.summary: Sorts heartbeasts into four temperaments, pure or aspected by another, and lists which creatures cannot be heartbeasts (domesticated animals, creatures with Might, those outside the Size limits). Includes the Size option for very small heartbeasts.
quotes: Creatures Smaller than a Weasel (Size –7)
Creatures Larger than an Aurochs (Size +3)

entries.title: Example Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Sidebar table assigning example animals to each heartbeast temperament and aspect.

entries.title: Plant Heartbeasts
entries.summary: Optional rule allowing an unusual plant 'heartbeast': the plant form can do only what a plant can do, and the character is likely to have Cyclic Magic.

entries.title: Statistics of Shapechangers
entries.summary: Seven-step procedure for combining human and animal statistics for a shapechanged magus: Characteristics, Cunning versus Intelligence, Size, Virtues and Flaws, General Abilities, communication, and wounds and experience.
quotes: If the human and the animal Characteristic are both negative, use the lower of the two.
If the human and the animal Characteristic are both positive, use the higher of the two.

entries.title: Bjornaer Magi and Familiars
entries.summary: Initiation into the Heartbeast mystery makes it impossible to bind a familiar, and a magus who has ever bound one cannot complete the ritual.
quotes: Any magus who has ever bound a familiar, even if it has since died, cannot successfully complete the Ritual of Twelve Years

entries.title: The Ritual of Twelve Years (Heartbeast initiation)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Heartbeast (Minor House Mystery)
entries.summary: The Initiation Script that grants the Heartbeast Virtue and Ability at level 1. It can never be repeated, its bonus depends on the temperaments of the witnesses, and it costs the ability to bind a familiar.
quotes: The Participation modifier provides +1 for every witness who has the same temperament as the probationer's heartbeast
Ease Factor: 15 (Minor Virtue known to the Mystagogue)

entries.title: Theriomorphy (Minor House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Theriomorphy (Minor House Mystery)
entries.summary: Lets a magus apply Qualities or Virtues of his heartbeast to his human form with a roll, along with partial physical change and Warping consequences. Includes the Initiation Script.
quotes: on a Stamina + Heartbeast roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Script Bonus: +6

entries.title: The Mystery of the Epitome (Major House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Mystery of the Epitome (Major House Mystery)
entries.summary: Perfects the heartbeast into a Beast of Virtue with a boosted Characteristic, a Mythic Feat usable at a Confidence cost, and immunity to shape-affecting Physical Flaws.
quotes: One Characteristic of the inner heartbeast (other than Intelligence) receives a permanent +3 bonus to the value of the base animal
at a cost of 1 confidence Point

entries.title: The Mystery of the Chimera (Major House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Mystery of the Chimera (Major House Mystery)
entries.summary: Transforms the heartbeast into a hybrid of two creatures, with constraints on what can be combined and a Size increase for the chimerical form.
quotes: A chimerical heartbeast is one size category larger than the outer heartbeast

entries.title: The Mystery of the Anima (Major House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Mystery of the Anima (Major House Mystery)
entries.summary: Transforms the heartbeast into a spiritual or elemental creature of the same shape and size, affected by the Form associated with its element instead of Animal.

entries.title: Characters of House Bjornaer (character creation)
entries.summary: Character creation guidance for a Bjornaer magus: choose the heartbeast first, then clan, with advice on Virtues and Flaws suited to the heartbeast and on why shapechanging Virtues are a hindrance in this House.

entries.title: Heartbeast (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: The Heartbeast Ability gives knowledge of the animal form, a Personality Trait named for the animal, and the power to change form. It cannot be learned from books and can only be taught by someone with the same temperament.
quotes: at a level equal to half the score in this Ability

entries.title: Criamon: The Enigma
entries.requires: House Criamon: Initiation into the Enigma
entries.summary: All Criamon magi have Enigmatic Wisdom 1 and may place experience in it at creation; the Ability helps comprehend Twilight but makes it more likely, and the House mysteries are divided into Paths.
quotes: All Criamon magi have a score of one in the Ability Enigmatic Wisdom, and may place experience points in it at character creation.

entries.title: Enigmatic Wisdom
entries.requires: House Criamon: Initiation into the Enigma
entries.summary: The Enigmatic Wisdom Ability adds to rolls to interpret dreams, riddles, phantasms and mysterious situations, and affects how often Criamon enter Twilight and how well they survive it.
quotes: Your score in this Ability is added to rolls to interpret dreams and riddles, and to understand phantasms and arcane or mysterious situations.

entries.title: Merinita: Faerie Magic
entries.requires: House Merinita: Initiation into Faerie Magic (must be touched by the fay)
entries.summary: Merinita initiates are attuned to Magic and Faerie auras (no Warping or extra botch dice from either) and gain special Ranges, Durations and Targets (Road, Bargain, Fire, Until (Condition), Year + 1, Bloodline) usable only by Faerie Magic characters.
quotes: A character may not be Initiated into this mystery unless she has been touched by the fay.
To calculate the level of a Bargain spell, calculate the level of the spell that takes effect when the bargain is broken, and add three magnitudes.

entries.title: Faerie Magic Ability
entries.requires: House Merinita: Initiation into Faerie Magic
entries.summary: The Faerie Magic Ability can stand in for Magic Theory when experimenting or working with faerie vis, raises the vis usable in a season for faerie vis, and adds botch dice that cause Warping Points without forcing Twilight checks.
quotes: The amount of vis you can use in a single season is equal to your (Magic Theory + Faerie Magic) x 2, so long as all of it is faerie vis.

versions.title: Faerie Magic Ability
versions.summary: Arcane Ability gained by Merinita who Initiate Faerie Magic; it enables charms and can substitute for Magic Theory in some lab work with faerie vis, with its own vis limit and botch-dice effects.
quotes: Faerie Magic may be substituted for Magic Theory when experimenting, when using faerie vis, or when practicing magic associated with the Faerie realm.
The amount of vis you can use in a single season is equal to your (Magic Theory + Faerie Magic) x 2, so long as all of it is faerie vis.
Add your score in Faerie Magic to the number of botch dice you roll in these conditions

entries.title: Verditius: Verditius Magic
entries.requires: House Verditius: Initiation into Verditius Magic
entries.summary: Verditius magi craft the item during its first season of enchanting, add Verditius Runes (their Philosophiae) to Shape and Material bonuses, add their Craft Ability to Lab Totals, reduce the vis needed to open the item, and need casting tools for Formulaic and Ritual spells.
quotes: a magus who does so may add his score in the relevant Craft Ability to all Lab Totals for enchanting that item
the number of pawns of vis needed to open the item for enchantment is reduced by the magus's Craft score, to a minimum of one pawn

entries.title: Monastic Roles and Positions
entries.requires: Playing a monk or nun with an office in a religious house
entries.summary: Describes the offices of a religious house (abbot or abbess, prior, terrar, cellarer, bursar, infirmarian, sacrist, hostillar, chancellor and others) with the Abilities, Social Status Virtue and reputation suited to each, useful for building monastic characters and contacts.
quotes: She has a reputation of level 4, either good or bad, in both the local community and the Church.

entries.title: Magic Theory Specializations of Magi Bonisagi
entries.summary: Three optional Magic Theory specializations (traditionalist, dabbler, harmonizer) available only to magi Bonisagi, each applying when a particular kind of research, spell invention or enchantment is undertaken.
quotes: You may choose traditionalist, dabbler, or harmonizer as a specialization for your Magic Theory

entries.title: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus
entries.summary: A community-based Reputation that every magus Bonisagi starts with, which grows through finished and published laboratory research and moves the magus up the House ranks. Describes how Acclaim points accrue and are sped up by being included in a folio.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every magus Bonisagi character receives at character generation.
The lucky author gains twice the Acclaim points listed on the following table if his research is included in a folio.

entries.title: Redcaps: Status and Role in the Order
entries.summary: Explains what a Redcap is: an unGifted member of House Mercere with the rights and privileges of a magus, a sigil, and a tradition of not voting at Tribunal, who acts like a Hermetic companion serving magi and performing duties magi find beneath them.
quotes: Redcaps may not have the Gift, but they do have full rights and privileges

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Followers of Belin
entries.requires: Redcap society: Followers of Belin (Legacy flaw)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of elite messengers descended from or adopted into Belin's line, with character requirements limiting them to humble, diligent Personality traits and the Legacy flaw.
quotes: they must take the Legacy flaw (see the Appendix, Virtues and Flaws)

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Pawnbrokers
entries.summary: A Redcap society that stores vis in distinctively shaped tokens; members may trade starting magic item levels for vis in their signature shape and receive a yearly pawn of vis from the House.
quotes: Pawnbroker Redcaps may trade two levels of their starting magic items for a pawn of vis in their signature shape

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Goliards
entries.requires: Redcap society: Goliards (Clerk or Educated, plus a Compulsion)
entries.summary: An artistic, hedonistic Redcap society; members must take Clerk or Educated and a Compulsion toward an inspirational vice, and commonly take Free Expression, Inspirational or a Hermetic Patron.
quotes: characters must take either Clerk or Educated

entries.title: Magical Merceres (Mercere Magi Privileges and Creation)
entries.summary: Describes Gifted Mercere magi: their lineage expectations, privileges (contracts for items, interest-free vis loans, free Portal use, support from Mercer Houses), yearly messenger season, casting taboos and the free Virtue they take at creation.
quotes: starting Mercere magi always take either Puissant Art (Creo) or Puissant Art (Muto) as their free Virtue
They may borrow up to 10p of vis from their House without paying interest

entries.title: Societas Merceris: Milvi Antiquiti
entries.requires: Redcap society: Milvi Antiquiti (Mutantum Magic for magi)
entries.summary: A Mutantes society that copies and lends ancient books to magi for a vis fee and carries them by shapeshifting into birds; magi members take Mutantum Magic and Redcap members usually learn Latin, Scribe and Magic Theory.
quotes: usually 1p a season or 3p a year

entries.title: Usurers (High-Interest Lending)
entries.summary: Describes higher interest rates charged by lenders who disregard the charge of usury, the social consequences, and advice for building a character who is an Usurer, including recommended Flaws and the Profession: Accountant Ability.
quotes: might ask closer to 50% interest on common loans

entries.title: Claiming the Name (Gauntlet by Certamen)
entries.summary: Explains the Tremere Gauntlet as a certamen challenge from apprentice to master for the title of magus, how it is staged and judged, and the ceremony of the birchwood wand that serves as the new magus's sigil.
quotes: It is all-but unheard of for an apprentice to win the role of magus by force

entries.title: Tremere Virtues and Flaws Guidance
entries.summary: House-specific character creation notes: all Tremere magi have a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen, plus which Virtues are common or inappropriate and which Flaws the House would not accept or would see as embarrassing.
quotes: All Tremere magi have a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen.

entries.title: Tremere Abilities
entries.summary: Lists the Abilities Tremere magi value for crisis and peacetime, such as Intrigue, Bargain, Penetration, Concentration, Parma Magica, Survival, Swim and Leadership.
quotes: Younger magi are expected to be able to fend for themselves on the Wizard's March

entries.title: Tremere Arts and Spells (Four-Art Duelists)
entries.summary: Explains why Tremere magi specialize in four Arts (to cope with a certamen opponent's veto of the first Art chosen) and which Arts they typically favor.
quotes: the other party in a duel can veto their rival's first choice of form or technique

entries.title: Leadworker (Katadesmoi and Penetration Bonuses)
entries.requires: Virtue: Leadworker (Minor, Hermetic); House Tremere tradition
entries.summary: Explains the leadworker's curse tablets and figurines and gives Penetration bonus table additions for a katadesmos tablet, a kolossos, and a kolossos containing a sympathetic connection, plus a free fixed Arcane Connection created from body material.
quotes: Katadesmos tablet, inscribed with the name of a victim (+2)
A Kolossos constructed with a sympathetic connection from the body of the victim imbedded in it (+3)

entries.title: Character Creation and the Mysteries
entries.requires: Starting a magus already Initiated into a Mystery cult (storyguide permission)
entries.summary: Rules for starting a magus who already holds House Mystery Virtues: they use ordinary Virtue and Flaw slots, and for older characters an Initiation costs the experience of one lab season. Includes the sidebar of common Script element bonuses.
quotes: subtracts 10 experience points from the character's total

entries.title: Outer Mystery of Verditius Magic
entries.summary: The initiation that every Verditius apprentice undergoes at the Forges of Hephaestus, granting the Verditius Magic Virtue, with its Target Level, Mystagogue requirement and Script bonus.
quotes: Mechanically, the Initiation Target Level is 15.
The Initiation Script has a bonus of +12

entries.title: Sensory Magic (Minor House Mystery)
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; Initiation: Sensory Magic (Minor House Mystery)
entries.summary: Special Targets that affect anyone sensing the caster, with the restrictions on these spells (Personal Range, no Intellego, no investing) and a Lab Total bonus from the Heartbeast Ability for inventing them.
quotes: the magus's Heartbeast Ability score is added to the Lab Total

entries.title: Mythic Blood (Birna and Great Beast bloodlines)
entries.summary: Explains how bearers of Birna's or a Great Beast's blood gain a Minor Magical Focus, a magical feat and a hereditary Personality Flaw, always with a bear heartbeast for Birna's line.

entries.title: Examples of Mythic Blood
entries.summary: Table of example Mythic Blood lines with the magical feat, Minor Magical Focus and Personality Flaw each confers.

entries.title: House Bjornaer Lore (Arcane Ability)
entries.summary: The Organization Lore for House Bjornaer, which also governs its Mystery rites. Each season spent initiating a Mystery gives experience in it.
quotes: every time a magus spends a season initiating a Mystery, he gains experience in House Bjornaer Lore from exposure

entries.title: House Acclaim
entries.summary: Flambeau's free Hermetic Reputation measuring prestige: gained through witnessed deeds, lost through inactivity or ignoble acts, never below zero.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every Flambeau magus gains at the start of play.
Loss of House Acclaim is handled by taking away experience points instead of adding them.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.21 House Acclaim (Bonisagus)

entries.title: Other Modifications (head binding)
entries.summary: Head binding and similar rituals done in infancy give an aptitude for a particular path, which is a bonus to the Initiation Script for the first station on that path.
quotes: This acts as a +3 bonus for his Initiation Script for the first station (Mystery Virtue) of that path.

entries.title: Designing Adulterations
entries.summary: Guidelines for designing adulterations as creatures or places, including their Magic Might range, how they bypass their creator's Aegis, and how adulterous regiones behave.
quotes: Each has a Magical Might score that ranges from 10, for minor adulterations, to 45, for the malignancies.

entries.title: Option: Variant House Benefits
entries.summary: Optional rule restricting the Flambeau free Minor House Virtue to Puissant Art (Ignem or Perdo), with substitutions allowed for the Ramius, Sebastian and Vilano schools.
quotes: This free Virtue must be either Puissant Art (Ignem) or Puissant Art (Perdo).

entries.title: Designing a League
entries.summary: Options a troupe can choose when building a league: desired stories, senior connections, headquarters, a shared Reputation bonus, assistance and a name, with a worked example.
quotes: All Reputations act as if they were 3 points higher, between colleagues.

entries.title: Less Intelligent Magi?
entries.summary: Optional character-creation note allowing Jerbiton magi with a Gentle Gift and a lower than usual Intelligence in sagas where the Gift is rare.
quotes: An Intelligence score less than +3 reflects a premium placed upon Gentle Giftedness by masters in House Jerbiton.

entries.title: Free Virtue (Jerbiton)
entries.summary: Jerbiton magi choose their own free House Virtue, limited to Minor Virtues relating to scholarship, art or dealing with people; includes suggested Virtues and Abilities and a ruling on Ability-linked Virtues.
quotes: This choice is limited to Minor Virtues that relate to scholarship, art, or interacting with people.
the magus does not lose this advantage when the Ability is used on non-mundane people

entries.title: Leper Magus (Vis from Leprotic Wounds)
entries.requires: House Tytalus; Virtue: Leper Magus (requires Flaw: Leprosy)
entries.summary: A Major Hermetic Virtue whose extended mechanic lets a leper magus take a wound to generate vis for one spell or lab activity, with limits on recovery, aging and how often it can be used.
quotes: By accepting a Light Wound, the magus can infuse a single magical working with three pawns of vis, of any Technique or Form.
A wound taken in this fashion must heal completely before the power may be used again, and any character using this power more than three times a year must make an extra Aging roll in winter.

entries.title: Titanoi (Mystery Cult of House Tytalus)
entries.summary: Describes the Titanoi cult of spirit summoners: the Major Magical Focus in Spirits and Abilities taught in apprenticeship, and the Mystery Virtues the cult can initiate.
quotes: The cult can Initiate the following Virtues: Hermetic Theurgy, Invocation Magic, Names of Power, Theurgic Spirit Familiar, and Student of Magic Realm.

entries.title: Leper Magi (Magi Aegroti)
entries.requires: House Tytalus; Virtue: Leper Magus; Flaw: Leprosy
entries.summary: Describes the lineage of leper magi, how later generations are found among lepers, their place in the Order, and the Virtues, Flaws and Magical Focus all of them have.
quotes: All magi aegroti must buy the Leper Magus Virtue and the Leprosy Flaw.

entries.title: Craft Magic (Rusticani)
entries.summary: Lets a character craft an object in place of casting an effect, with shape and material bonuses capped by his Craft score, and also to make charged items and lesser enchantments of vis-containing objects without spending a season. Four applications, each with its own time and level rules and worked examples.
quotes: though this bonus cannot exceed his Craft score
Use the character's Casting Total or the result of the Supernatural Ability roll as if it were a Lab Total to determine the effect's level and the number of charges
the level of the invested effect cannot exceed five times the number of pawns of vis in the object

related.text: RoP: The Divine pp.137-138 Craft Amulets

entries.title: Cabal Legacy — Minor Hermetic Story Flaw
entries.summary: The Story Flaw that lets a new magus begin play already Initiated, taking cult Virtues and Ordeal Flaws as part of the normal ten points of Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: It allows a magus character to be designed with cult Virtues as normal Virtues, part of the standard ten Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Astrological Cyclic Magic — Minor Hermetic Virtue or Flaw
entries.summary: Lets Cyclic Magic follow astrological cycles of the zodiac, raising the bonus or penalty when the cycle covers less of the year.
quotes: The bonus or penalty is increased to 5.
The bonus or penalty is increased to 6.

entries.title: Hermetic Rune Magic: Rune Duration and Inscription Target
entries.summary: The extended mechanic behind the Hermetic Rune Magic Virtue: the Rune Duration and Inscription Target, how and how fast runes are inscribed, casting-total modifiers for hiding or omitting the name and description, the craft-roll alternative, and the drawbacks (a lasting Arcane Connection and a Warping Point for the target).
quotes: This Duration is equivalent to Moon, adding three magnitudes to a spell's base level.
If the magus does not inscribe his name into the inscription, he receives a –5 penalty.

entries.title: Ability: Rune Magic
entries.requires: Rune Magic study or Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic
entries.summary: The Arcane Ability covering knowledge of runes: their symbolism, formulating and encrypting rune-script, and copying books on rune magic.
quotes: hiding runes, identifying rune magic, runes associated with a particular Art.

entries.title: Hunters' Arts (Practice and Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Overview of the Hunters' Arts, a splintered hedge tradition with three Practice Arts (Scry, Ban, Slay) each paired with a Foe Art. Explains how the Arts are bought as Virtues, how the first Foe Art comes free, how experience is gained and why most hunters can only use their Arts on one kind of foe.
quotes: There are three Practices that are akin to Hermetic Techniques: Scry, Ban, and Slay.

Practice Arts are bought as Major Supernatural Virtues, whereas Foe Arts are Minor Supernatural Virtues, but a character buying his first Practice Art as a Virtue gets one free Foe Art at no additional Virtue point cost.

entries.title: (Foe) Art (Virtue and rules for Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Describes the Foe Art Virtue: what counts as a valid foe, the storyguide's say over its breadth, and that Foe Arts are Difficult Arts that advance like Abilities and must be combined with a Practice Art.
quotes: A foe must have some supernatural power: wholly mundane groups cannot be foes.
(Foe) Arts are Difficult Arts, meaning that they are treated as any other Art except that they use the Ability Advancement Table rather than the Art Advancement Table.

entries.title: The Lineage of Irmele
entries.summary: Describes a wandering Bonisagus lineage in the Rhine whose members travel as peregrinatores, tend to weather magic, are strong in Arts and rich in vis, and often rely on spontaneous magic for lack of a laboratory.
quotes: Once they achieve the status of master, they will, unlike others, typically remain a peregrinator for a couple of decades

related.text: Laws of Hospitality and the Peregrinatores

entries.title: The Perthean Compact and Personal Vis Sources
entries.requires: Normandy Tribunal; Hermetic Virtue granting a personal vis source
entries.summary: Explains how a magus's own bodily vis is exempt from the Perthean Compact and how a character with an external personal vis source can justify it in a Normandy saga.
quotes: any vis that is generated by the person of a magus (in his hair, blood, and so forth) is the sole possession of that magus, and not subject to the Perthean Compact

entries.title: Priests' Wives and Mistresses
entries.requires: Playing a priest's wife or companion
entries.summary: Character-option advice for a woman living with a priest: the troupe decides whether the union counts as a valid marriage and whether it is a Dark Secret, and suggests roles in the parish such as a sacristan's wife.
quotes: Troupes with a female player character who lives with a priest should decide whether the priest and his wife consider themselves to be living under valid vows of marriage, or whether they believe themselves to be in a sinful relationship.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.81-82

entries.title: Covenant-Bred Childhood
entries.summary: A childhood package for characters raised in a covenant, giving experience in Area Lore: Covenant, Latin and Organization Lore: Order of Hermes among others.
quotes: This childhood is only available to characters with the Covenant Upbringing Personality Flaw.

entries.title: Feral Childhood
entries.summary: A childhood package for characters raised wild, giving experience in survival and animal-related Abilities.
quotes: This childhood is only available to characters with the Feral Upbringing Flaw.

entries.title: Failed Apprentice Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for a former apprentice whose Gift was lost, with Characteristics, Virtue and Flaw suggestions reflecting remnants of the Gift, packages, and sample Ability scores at several ages.

entries.title: Role-Bound Ferryman Grog Template
entries.summary: A template for grogs who are bound to a single role or device and cannot serve any other purpose, with creation notes, a training-package set for the example ferryman and sample Ability scores at three ages.
quotes: In addition, role-bound grogs must have a Profession or Craft Ability that defines them.

entries.title: Time-Lost Witness Grog Template
entries.summary: Rules and advice for characters displaced in time by faeries, including why time-lost magi are not supported, the difficulties such characters face, and an example set of Roman legionaries with sample Ability scores.
quotes: These grogs require the Warrior Virtue, and must take the Worthless Abilities Flaw.

entries.title: Animal Grogs
entries.summary: Introduces animals as grog characters, with guidance on which Sizes and kinds of animal make the best player characters.
quotes: creatures between the Sizes of –3 and +2

entries.title: Animal Physical Form
entries.summary: Explains what an animal body prevents (grasping and using tools) and grants (natural protection, natural weapons and abilities like flight or swimming), and that listed Quality modifiers are not applied.
quotes: which grant an intrinsic Protection of at least 1

entries.title: Animal Cunning Instead of Intelligence
entries.summary: Animals have Cunning rather than Intelligence, act by instinct and Personality Traits, cannot reason logically, and must take the Restricted Learning Flaw.
quotes: The Cunning characteristic possessed by beasts means that they act largely through estimation (also called instinct), and are ruled by their Personality Traits.

entries.title: Animal Language Abilities
entries.summary: Animals cannot speak, have no automatic Native Language, learn human languages slowly depending on Cunning, and have a species Language Ability that cannot be raised with experience.
quotes: an animal always has a Source Quality of (4 + Cunning)

entries.title: Animal Grog Characteristics and Size
entries.summary: Gives how Size, the Large Virtue and Small Frame Flaw affect an animal grog, the penalties to Presence and Communication when dealing with humans by animal type, and how Size adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: After Characteristic points have been decided, add twice the character's Size to her Strength, and subtract the character's Size from her Quickness.

entries.title: Animal Grog Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Lists the intrinsic Flaws every animal grog has without gaining points, the required Restricted Learning Flaw, suitable Social Status options, and how Animal Ken substitutes for a Language Ability.
quotes: Animal grogs suffer from the effects of the No Hands and Mute Flaws

entries.title: Animal Grog Abilities and Experience
entries.summary: Describes the starting experience animal grogs receive for their pre-adult life, their free animal Language Ability, yearly experience, early aging and typical Abilities.
quotes: An animal grog receives 120 experience points for his pre-adult life

entries.title: Tremere Specialist Roles
entries.summary: Introduces the specialist roles in which Tremere magi are trained to serve the House, noting that they cannot have magical focuses other than certamen and so hire other Houses for specialized research and item construction.
quotes: Tremere magi cannot have magical focuses other than certamen, so they hire magi from other Houses to provide specialized services.

entries.title: Hedge wizard as a Grog
entries.summary: A very minor unGifted hedge wizard can be a grog with a few Minor Virtues representing his powers.
quotes: created as a grog character who has up to three Minor Virtues to represent his powers

entries.title: Jewish Grogs Must Take Outsider
entries.summary: Jewish grogs must take the Minor Outsider Flaw and live in a Jewish community or covenant, since a Jew outside such places is too conspicuous to be a background character.
quotes: Jewish grogs must take the Outsider Minor Flaw

entries.title: The Rottweiler (playable dog grog)
entries.requires: Storyguide approval; a magus who keeps Rottweilers
entries.summary: Optional rules for playing a faerie-blooded hunting dog as a grog: it uses Cunning in place of Intelligence, receives a fixed package of Virtues and Flaws, and has its age and aging rolls scaled to dog years. Some have faerie blood that slows aging or grants Second Sight.
quotes: the hound may be created as a normal character, except that it has Cunning instead of Intelligence
Their bite has the same combat statistics as a dagger.
Calculate their age (and experience) as for a human, and use this age for making aging rolls

entries.title: Mythic Companions (overview)
entries.requires: Troupe approval and a Mythic Companion Virtue
entries.summary: Introduces Mythic Companions, non-Hermetic characters such as non-Hermetic wizards or supernatural warriors whose power approaches a magus's. They are normally played as an alternative to a magus, and the troupe may disallow them.

versions.title: Mythic Companions (Non-Hermetic Magicians)
versions.summary: Describes Mythic Companions as non-Gifted characters who can fill the role of non-Hermetic magicians, with a Special Virtue that replaces The Gift and a Virtue point allowance based on Flaws taken.
quotes: Instead, a Mythic Companion has a Special Virtue akin to The Gift, which grants a Minor Virtue at no cost, and then two Virtue points for every point of Flaw he takes.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.104

versions.title: Mythic Companions (creation rules)
versions.summary: Rules for building a Mythic Companion, a non-Hermetic character of near-magus power: a status Free Virtue, a free Minor Virtue, extra Flaws allowed, and a minimum Ability set.
quotes: In addition, you may take up to ten points of Flaws, and each point of Flaws is worth two points of Virtues.
This produces a maximum of 21 points of Virtues and 10 points of Flaws.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages - Blood of Heroes

versions.title: Mythic Companions
versions.summary: Character-creation rules for Gift-less companions who rival magi: a special Free Virtue, a bonus Virtue point, Flaws worth double, and a list of the new Infernal Virtues available to them.
quotes: each of these Flaws is worth twice as many Virtues
can have as many as 21 points of Virtues
Mythic Companions may not take The Gift.

versions.title: Mythic Companions
versions.summary: Introduces Mythic Companions as a character type closer in power to magi than ordinary companions, who can never have the Gift, with advice to the storyguide on how many such characters a saga should hold.
quotes: Characters with Blood of Heroes are Mythic Companions, a new character type.

entries.title: Mythic Companions (creation)
entries.summary: How to build a Mythic Companion: a free status Virtue, a free Minor Virtue, extra Virtue points for each Flaw point, and an agreed minimum set of Abilities.
quotes: each point of Flaws is worth two points of Virtues
As for Hermetic magi, this set of Abilities should come to a total of 90 experience points.

entries.title: Faerie Doctors as Mythic Companions
entries.summary: Required Virtues, Flaws and minimum Ability scores for a magus-level faerie doctor, plus how to play a lesser faerie doctor who is not a Mythic Companion.
quotes: Curse-Throwing 4

entries.title: Nephilim
entries.summary: Mythic Companion type for divine giants: required Virtues, the Flaw points that pay for them, and minimum Ability scores. Recommended for high-powered sagas.
quotes: Nephilim must take five points of Flaws to pay for these virtues and may take an additional five points of Flaws, which grants a further ten points of Virtues.

entries.title: Spirit Votary
entries.summary: Mythic Companion type for a worshiper of a magical spirit: required Virtues, a compulsory Pagan Flaw and minimum Ability scores.
quotes: Spiritual Pact (Major, Supernatural)

entries.title: Blood of Heroes (Hero Characters)
entries.requires: Virtue: Blood of Heroes (free Virtue; House Mercere)
entries.summary: Creation rules for hero characters: they have no Gift, count as Mythic Companions, may take Heroic Virtues and Flaws, gain double Virtue points from Flaws, must take Heroic Personality, and are normally Redcaps; the storyguide may veto overpowered heroes.
quotes: each point of Flaws that you take during character creation balances two points of Virtues instead of one

entries.title: Heroic (Access to Heroic Virtues and Flaws)
entries.requires: Blood of Heroes, Legacy flaw, or Mythic Blood
entries.summary: Defines which characters count as Heroic and may therefore take Heroic Virtues and Flaws, with room for storyguide discretion in other circumstances.
quotes: Only "Heroic" characters can take Heroic Virtues and Flaws.

entries.title: Mythic Companion: Perfecti
entries.summary: Template for creating a Cathar Perfectus Mythic Companion with required Virtues and Flaws, a remaining Flaw budget, and minimum Ability scores.
quotes: characters must spend 50 of their starting experience points to achieve these scores in the following Abilities

entries.title: Mythic Companion: Zahids
entries.summary: Character-creation template for ascetic Sufi zahids, listing required Virtues, Flaws, Social Status choices and minimum Ability scores.
quotes: All zahids must begin with the free Virtue Zahid, a Mythic Companion Virtue.
Zahid characters must spend 90 experience points on the following Abilities.

entries.title: Mythic Companion: Kabbalist
entries.summary: Character-creation template for kabbalists: favored Abilities, required Virtues and Flaws, minimum Ability scores, and the Tree of Life table of Sefirot levels.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Ceremony, Gematria, Kabbalah, Merkavah
The kabbalist must start with the following minimum Ability scores:

entries.title: Mythic Companion: The Diabolist
