entries.summary: How a character becomes a diabolist through a ceremony with a demon, and character creation for a Diabolist Mythic Companion with required Virtues and a split of Infernal Virtues.
quotes: To become a diabolist, a character must only participate in a short ceremony with a demon
This leaves him with ten points of Flaws to spend, which balance out as many as 20 more points of Virtues.

entries.title: Mythic Companion: The Summoner
entries.summary: Character creation for a Summoner Mythic Companion: required Summoner and Summoning Virtues plus one free Minor Virtue, with the background of sorcerers and their ghostly mentors.
quotes: Summoning (Major, Goetic Art)

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Mythic Companions
entries.summary: Character-creation limits for Mythic Companions, who get extra Virtue points per Flaw point, a defining Free Virtue and a free Minor Virtue.
quotes: You make take up to 10 points of Flaws, and 2 points of Virtues for every 1 point of Flaws, for a maximum of 20 points of Virtues

entries.title: The Maestro: A Mythic Companion
entries.summary: Rules for building a maestro, a mythic artist companion: the special Maestro Virtue gives extra Virtue points per Flaw point and a free artistic Virtue, the character is tied to one of the four realms, may not have the Gift, must take a Susceptibility Flaw and may learn any Ability at creation.
quotes: The character must take the special Virtue: Maestro, which then allows him to have twice as many points of Virtues as he has points of Flaws.
The player may then purchase up to 10 points of Flaws for the character, with each point spent allowing him to purchase two points of Virtues.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.81-82
Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.103-109

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Cult of Heroes
entries.requires: Redcap society: Cult of Heroes (Blood of Heroes for hero characters; Mythic Blood or Mercurian Magic and Pagan for magi)
entries.summary: A society that raises exceptional children as heroes; hero characters take the Blood of Heroes virtue, may trade starting magic item levels for Characteristic increases, and Cult magi may substitute Mastered Spells for Puissant Art.
quotes: Either type may exchange 10 levels of effects in their starting magic items for a +1 increase to any of their negative Characteristics.

entries.title: Hedge wizard as a Mythic Companion
entries.summary: A more powerful unGifted hedge wizard built as a Mythic Companion with the free Mythic Companion Status, extra Flaws balancing double their value in Virtues, and an extra Minor Virtue.
quotes: The character also receives an extra Minor Virtue at no cost. This means that the Mythic Companion character has a maximum of 21 points of Virtues.

entries.title: Faerie Doctors as Mythic Companions
entries.summary: Character-building rules for playing a faerie doctor, either as a Mythic Companion with the Faerie Doctor Special Virtue and doubled Virtue points per Flaw, or as a Gifted or ordinary character, with compulsory Virtues and Flaws and Favored Abilities.
quotes: receives 2 points to spend on Virtues for every point he spends on Flaws

related.text: ArM5 p.28 Virtue and Flaw balance

entries.title: Heroic descent: Virtues and Flaws of Greek heroes
entries.requires: Virtue: Mythic Blood or Hero's Birthright Power
entries.summary: Lists famous Greek heroes and the Virtues and Flaws their descendants are likely to inherit, as guidance for building heroic bloodlines.
quotes: His descendants are highly likely to have a Greater Immunity to Metal and the Fury Flaw.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, page 105 (Hero's Birthright)

entries.title: Child Characters
entries.summary: Child characters are built normally and then take age-based modifiers to Characteristics and Size, with some Virtues and Flaws applying only as they grow up.
quotes: To generate a child, use the normal rules, and then modify all Characteristics as follows:

entries.title: Devil Child
entries.summary: Mythic Companion type for the creation of a demon: required Virtues and Flaws, a bonus of extra Virtue points, and a recommendation for high-powered sagas.
quotes: Devil Children may take three more points of Virtues at no cost (to balance the compulsory Major Flaw with six Virtue points)

entries.title: Mythic Companion: Devil Child
entries.summary: Character creation for a Devil Child Mythic Companion: the Devil Child Free Virtue replaces The Gift, with required Virtues and Flaws and extra Virtue points.
quotes: It also grants a free Minor Virtue, allowing a maximum of 21 points of Virtues for 10 points of Flaws.
Devil Children may take three more points of Virtues at no cost

entries.title: Abusive Lengths of Apprenticeship
entries.summary: An optional rule giving longer apprenticeships for certain guilds, and how the extra years of experience are earned and applied.
quotes: Instead of the regular seven years of apprenticeship, use the lengths listed on the table below.

entries.title: Guild Apprentices (Advancement and Apprentice Piece)
entries.requires: Virtue: Guild Apprentice (or Craftsman for non-guild apprentices)
entries.summary: Rules for apprentice characters: the Virtue required, how the seven years of apprenticeship translate into seasons of experience and which Abilities may receive it, and the apprentice piece test that ends the apprenticeship.
quotes: Starting guild apprentice characters must buy the Minor Social Status Virtue Guild Apprentice.
an apprentice character receives two seasons of Exposure experience, one season of Practice experience, and one season of Training a year
The apprentice makes a Primary Characteristic + Craft Ability + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Failed Apprentice Training Package
entries.summary: A package for characters who were trained as magi but never learned the Arts, giving Hermetic-flavoured Abilities.
quotes: Five Years: +5 Artes Liberales, +5 Code of Hermes, +5 Concentration, +5 Finesse, +10 Latin, +25 Magic Theory, +15 Organization Lore: Order of Hermes, +5 Penetration

entries.title: Joining the Templars as a Child
entries.summary: Children may enter the Templars as novices once old enough to bear arms, with each local commander judging fitness; orphans are usually directed elsewhere.
quotes: Ages of admission of children range from 11 to 14.

entries.title: Apprentices of House Bonisagus
entries.summary: How House Bonisagus apprentices are chosen and trained, and the distinct gauntlets of the two branches: the Theoretical Interview for magi Bonisagi and a solo journey for magi Trianomae.

entries.title: Fostering Apprentices
entries.summary: Magi Bonisagi swap apprentices for a year of Ability training and then a stint of lab assistance, a procedure that gives both apprentices Teaching and Profession: Scribe and improves Latin and Magic Theory.
quotes: At the end of two years, both apprentices should have scores of 2 in Teaching and Profession: Scribe, as well as improved scores in Latin and Magic Theory.

entries.title: Guernicus Apprenticeship and Gauntlet
entries.summary: Describes how Guernicus apprentices are trained (moral philosophy, investigation Abilities such as Folk Ken, Awareness and Intrigue) and how the House gauntlet tests them, including a secret test of honesty that decides whether the apprentice may become a Quaesitor.
quotes: If an apprentice is dishonest three times, he will be allowed to enter House Guernicus, but not as a Quaesitor.

entries.title: The Apprenticeship of a Bjornaer Magus
entries.summary: Explains the two phases of Bjornaer training, the shared sleeping years under the whole sept and the awakened years under a single master after the heartbeast is awakened, and how this fits the Code of Hermes apprenticeship length.
quotes: an apprentice will receive 15 seasons of training over 15 years before joining the Order

entries.title: Bjornaer Magi and Shapeshifting Apprentices
entries.requires: House Bjornaer; character with Skinchanger or Shapeshifter Virtue
entries.summary: How each clan treats apprentices who can already shapeshift, and what a known shapeshifter must accept (the Secret Name Mystery first, and loss of the shapechanging Virtue as the Ordeal for the Inner Mystery). Suggests Dark Secret if the ability is hidden.

entries.title: Experiences of Apprenticeship (Bjornaer)
entries.summary: Shows how an apprenticeship differs depending on whether the child is found just before or just after a Gathering of Twelve Years, including how late the heartbeast awakens in the second case.

entries.title: Riddles (Criamon apprenticeship and Enigmatic Wisdom)
entries.summary: Explains how each Criamon apprentice receives fifteen riddles to ponder, which builds the Enigmatic Wisdom mindset, the Riddle of the Magus that replaces the Gauntlet, and how apprentices choose a path.
quotes: At the beginning of her apprenticeship, each Criamon apprentice is given fifteen riddles

entries.title: Verditius Apprenticeship and Gauntlet
entries.summary: How a Verditius apprentice is initiated into the Outer Mystery while the Arts are opened, what the master must know to do it, and how the apprentice's Gauntlet is a masterpiece enchanted item made in an extra season.
quotes: Verditius magi must also have a score of 2 in Verditius Cult Lore.
The parens supplies the necessary vis, and gives the apprentice a season to work unaided in his laboratory.

entries.title: Tytalan Apprenticeship
entries.summary: Describes how House Tytalus trains apprentices, from the education before opening the Arts through the harsh years of training and the Book of Instruction, and what happens to apprentices who fail to react to it.
quotes: During the next 15 years, the apprentice's life is exceptionally hard.

entries.title: The Apprentice's Gauntlet
entries.summary: How a Tytalan apprenticeship ends: the apprentice must force his master to accept him as a magus in an eristic moot, with consequences (Self Confident, Weak Parens, Tormenting Master) depending on how and when the Gauntlet is passed.
quotes: The apprentice passes his Gauntlet if he can make his master accept him as an equal.
An apprentice who succeeds in killing his master at any point in his apprenticeship is elevated to the status of magus immediately, regardless of the state of his training.

entries.title: Joint Training of Apprentices
entries.requires: House Ex Miscellanea: Lineage of Pralix
entries.summary: Describes the arrangement in which a Pralician teaches Hermetic magic to a hedge wizard's apprentice in exchange for laboratory assistance, producing an apprentice trained in both traditions.
quotes: for every season the Pralican spends teaching Hermetic magic to her colleague's apprentice, she gets two seasons of the apprentice's assistance in the laboratory

entries.title: The Initiated Apprentice And Beyond
entries.requires: Parens belonging to a Mystery Cult, with troupe permission
entries.summary: Rules for starting characters who are already Initiates, and for advancing a magus through Initiations as background experience (one season per Quest plus one for the Initiation itself), including how to sketch a Script quickly.
quotes: The whole process takes one full season per Quest, and one for the Initiation itself.
each season of Initiation or Questing means the character loses 10 experience points from the yearly 30

entries.title: Opening the Gift (hedge traditions)
entries.summary: A season-long ritual in which a Gifted master Opens an apprentice's Gift to the tradition; if the apprentice already has Supernatural Abilities or Arts, an Opening Total is compared with an Opening Ease Factor, with a worked example.
quotes: It takes one season to Open The Gift, which occupies both the apprentice and the master for the whole season.
Opening Ease Factor: twice apprentice's Supernatural Ability + Art scores (+ 12 if Gift already Open)
unless the Opening Total exceeds twice the Opening Ease Factor the apprentice loses his existing Supernatural Ability and Art Scores

entries.title: Flawed Opening of The Gift
entries.summary: A master who lacks competence in the tradition's Arts and Abilities passes on a Flaw to the apprentice for each shortfall.
quotes: the character must have a score of at least 2 in each Supernatural Ability and Art of the tradition

entries.title: Vitkir as Characters
entries.requires: Tradition: Vitkir (The Gift, apprenticed rune master)
entries.summary: Character creation for vitkir: designed like magi with The Gift, a long apprenticeship in the 24 runes, set starting experience and rune script levels, minimum Abilities, virtue and flaw limits, and the Vitki Social Status.
quotes: They receive a total of 240 experience points for these years of specialized study
120 levels of rune scripts
A score of 10 in a single rune is the practical maximum for a character who has just finished his apprenticeship.

entries.title: Modified Runes (Younger Futhark and Futhorc)
entries.requires: Tradition: Vitkir (Younger Futhark or Anglo-Saxon Futhorc)
entries.summary: Variant rune alphabets that use the same magic system: the Younger Futhark has fewer runes, so fewer are opened at the start; the Futhorc has more characters, which dilutes experience and power.
quotes: The magic of the Younger Futhark uses only 16 of the 24 runes (as shown in the insert)

entries.title: The Younger Futhark
entries.summary: Reference table for the 16-rune Younger Futhark, listing the Elder Futhark runes that are missing and how each remaining rune maps to its Elder equivalent.
quotes: the runemasters eventually settled on a set of 16 runes instead of the original 24

entries.title: Lost Children
entries.summary: Template for abandoned children who became ageless Magical beings, designed with a child's Size and Characteristic penalties.
quotes: so to play one you should design a character with the Size and Characteristics penalties of a child

entries.title: The Sibyllides (children of sibyls)
entries.summary: Describes the children of sibyls as magic kin who always have prophecy- or sight-related powers and who must report back to their mother periodically.
quotes: They are obligated to return to their mother's home every decade to report to her what they have learned about the world

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 89 (magic kin)
Realms of Power: Magic, page 95 (Warders of Mystery)

entries.title: Retrieved Changelings
entries.summary: Describes how parents can retrieve a stolen child by tricking the changeling faerie into revealing itself, and what a retrieved child tends to gain, such as Second Sight or Faerie Blood of the kidnappers' variety.

entries.title: The Dhampir (child of a vampire)
entries.requires: Being a child of a vampire (Dhampir Virtue)
entries.summary: Describes dhampiri, the hunters sired by vampires, who charge a fee that by tradition cannot be bargained down and who will themselves rise as vampires after death unless precautions are taken.
quotes: dhampiri carry a dark secret: that they themselves will become vampires following their death

entries.title: Guild Member Ages and Abilities
entries.summary: A table of suggested ages, Craft scores and secondary Abilities for each guild rank, used as a guideline when creating guild member characters.
quotes: Journeyman | 5 | 2 (Bargain)

entries.title: Journeymen (Requirements, Contracts and Promotion)
entries.summary: Describes journeyman characters: the Virtue, age and Craft requirements, how the wage contract is bargained for, joining a guild in another town via a harder apprentice piece, the cost and vote needed to become a master, and annual dues.
quotes: Journeymen characters must buy the Minor Social Status Virtue Journeyman.
a Communication + Bargain + (Age / 10, rounded up) stress roll against a variable Ease Factor
The Ease Factor for this piece should be increased from 9 to 12.

entries.title: Guild Masters
entries.summary: Requirements for master characters and how many workers a master can employ, with a Labor Point penalty for being understaffed.
quotes: Master characters must have the Minor Social Status Virtue Guild Master.
A master can employ a number of apprentices and journeymen equal to his Leadership score.
Subtract 3 Labor Points for every absent worker from the number of Labor Points the master accrues in a season.

entries.title: Senior Masters
entries.summary: Requirements for senior master characters and how many workshops they can operate.
quotes: Character senior masters may effectively operate a number of workshops equal to one half their Leadership score rounded up.

entries.title: Guild Dean
entries.summary: How deans are selected and removed, the starting requirements for a dean character, and the stipend a dean receives from his guild.
quotes: he should be at least 50 years of age, have a Craft Ability of at least, 7 and have Bargain, Leadership, and Guild Lore scores of 5 or more
This stipend runs from 20 to 40 pounds, and can include properties like a large house or an additional workshop.

entries.title: Guild Members (Ranks, Roster and Required Abilities)
entries.summary: Introduces guild ranks, the guild roster, and the Abilities guild members need, including minimum Guild Lore scores by rank.
quotes: Journeymen need at least a Guild Lore score of 1, masters need a 2, and senior masters and deans must have a Guild Lore score of 3.

entries.title: Craftswomen and the Male Guild Sponsor
entries.requires: Female guild character (Virtue: Male Guild Sponsor)
entries.summary: Explains how women are restricted in guilds and the ways they enter them through a father's or husband's name on the roster, and how the Male Guild Sponsor Virtue lets a female character join any guild in a saga.
quotes: allows female characters to participate in any guild of the player's choice
Even if a woman gains the status of a master, she is legally forbidden the opportunity to be a guild official.

entries.title: Service Guilds
entries.summary: Service guilds follow the craft guild rules, with Profession replacing Craft for ability requirements and labor pools replacing workshops.
quotes: Replace the requirement for specific scores in a Craft Ability with a requirement for the same score in a Profession Ability.

entries.title: Natural Philosopher Training Package
entries.summary: An academic package that grants Philosophiae experience and a number of natural-philosophy formulae instead of a third Ability.
quotes: Five Years: +40 Philosophiae, 7 formulae

entries.title: Designing Beasts of Virtue
entries.summary: Beasts of Virtue use the Chapter 4 magical character rules with set Inherited Virtues and Flaws and no physical-defect Flaws.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Magic Animal; Essential Virtue (Major or Minor)

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Concept
entries.summary: Rules for Characteristics, the required Magic Animal and Essential Virtues, and permitted Virtues and Flaws when creating a Beast of Virtue.
quotes: You have 7 points to spend on Characteristics, just as other characters.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: How a Beast of Virtue's season of life sets its age and how its experience points must be spent on species Abilities.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Natural weapons, Protection and species Qualities for animals, and the reminder to subtract Size from initial Might.
quotes: Remember to subtract the Size of a Beast of Virtue from the initial Might score to get the final Might score.

entries.title: Characters with Might Scores
entries.summary: Special rules for characters with a Might Score: no Virtues tied to another realm, magic resistance from several sources does not stack, immunity to Warping, and immunity to supernatural backlashes of their own realm.
quotes: Characters with a Might Score are immune to all Warping (see Warping and Non-Humans, page 389).
these totals do not stack

entries.title: Magic Character Creation
entries.summary: Introduces the procedure for designing characters that begin play with Magic Might, such as familiars, ghostly warders or magical servants.

entries.title: Magic Character Creation Summary
entries.summary: Four-step summary of making a magic character: pick a concept (true form, Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Size), determine season and Abilities, set Magic Might and choose Qualities and Inferiorities, then add finishing touches.
quotes: Characteristics: 7 points assigned as in standard Detailed Character Creation (see ArM5 page 29), no Characteristic more than +3 or less than -3.
A spring character receives 120 experience points, a summer character receives 360, an autumn character receives 720, and a winter character receives 1200.

entries.title: Magic Character Concept
entries.summary: First step of making a magic character: choose its true form, assign base Characteristics, decide whether it is intelligent, take the Special Virtue for its type plus a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, other Virtues and Flaws, and set Size, which adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: you should begin with all eight scores at 0 and assign 7 points to them
adding two times Size to Strength, and subtracting Size from Quickness

entries.title: Magic Animal Characters
entries.summary: Rules for building a magic animal character from a mundane animal's stats: innate No Hands and Mute equivalents, required minimum Abilities, and a Size adjustment to Magic Might.
quotes: you must subtract the character's Size from its Might Score, or add to it if Size is negative

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Magic Human Characters
entries.summary: Magic humans are designed like ordinary human characters but always look monstrous, suffering a social penalty with mundane humans and animals; magi are better designed normally and given a transformation Virtue later.
quotes: giving them a –6 to all social interactions with mundane humans or animals

entries.title: Magic Thing Characters
entries.summary: Magic things draw their Might from Size according to a minimum-Size table, can grow in Might by joining a larger entity, move slowly, are not blocked by Magic Resistance unless using an active supernatural effect, and always have Temporary Might.
quotes: The following chart shows the minimum Size required for each level of Might Score.
Magic things always have Temporary Might
All magic thing characters receive the No Fatigue Quality at no cost.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition p.64 Hermetic Empowerment
The Mysteries Revised Edition p.66 Spirit Familiar
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.134 Bind Magical Creatures

entries.title: Magic Spirit Characters
entries.summary: Magic spirits are designed from a physical form's Characteristics but are insubstantial, can be affected only by beings of the same form, are immortal unless their true form is destroyed, and always have an innate Magical Air.
quotes: Magic spirits always have an innate Magical Air that is very difficult for them to overcome.

entries.title: Magic Character Season
entries.summary: Season replaces age for magic characters and determines starting experience points: spring, summer, autumn or winter stages of development, with Abilities bought according to Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: Season is a new statistic that replaces age for magic characters
| Winter | 1200 |

entries.title: Magic Might (character creation)
entries.summary: Choose a Magic Might Score and Form from a table by saga power level and role (grog, companion, magus); the Might Score also gives an equal number of points for Magic Qualities, and is subtracted from all Advancement Totals.
quotes: You must subtract the character's Might Score from all Advancement Totals
Minor Qualities cost 1 point, and Major Qualities cost 3 points.

entries.title: Magic Character Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Final steps: at least three Personality Traits, Reputations, starting Confidence for eligible characters, an Essential Trait for its true form, combat scores, equipment and inherent vis.
quotes: (this is typically equal to its Might Score divided by 5, rounded up)

entries.title: Qualities and Inferiorities
entries.summary: Magic Qualities and Inferiorities are the Virtue and Flaw equivalents for characters with a Might Score; they are bought with points equal to Might, need not balance, and grogs may not take Major ones.
quotes: A character starts with a set number of Quality points equal to its Might Score

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.104-109 Heroic Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Major Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Qualities a magic character can buy, including Fatigue Mastery, Focus, Greater and Ritual Powers (with their Might costs and Initiative), Gentle Air, Gifted, Gigantic with its Size table, Improved Characteristic, Natural Appearance, No Fatigue and Vis Mastery.
quotes: The power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2)

entries.title: Minor Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Qualities, such as Form Resistance, Gift of Speech, the Improved Abilities, Attack, Damage, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Powers, Recovery and Soak options, Lesser Power, Minor Virtue and Personal Power.
quotes: Personal Powers have a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Improved Abilities: You gain 50 experience points, which may be spent on any Abilities or Arts that the character can learn.

entries.title: Major Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Inferiorities, such as Acclimation Prone, Major Flaw, Miniature with its Size table, Monstrous Appearance, Reduced Characteristic and Temporary Might, which ties wounds to Might Points and vis.
quotes: When the character is injured, it loses Might Points equal to the penalty of the wound

entries.title: Minor Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Inferiorities, such as Limited Gestures, Movement and Speech, Minor Flaw, the Reduced Abilities, Attack, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Power and Soak options, and Susceptible to Deprivation.
quotes: Reduced Abilities: Subtract 50 experience points from the character's existing Abilities

entries.title: Magic Kin
entries.summary: Introduces magic kin lineages that can be used as templates for magic characters, each with Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws to take at character creation.
quotes: that characters designed to belong to that family should strongly consider taking during character creation

entries.title: Atlanteans
entries.summary: Template for ocean-dwelling Atlantean characters with water-based Inherited Virtues, an exile Flaw and powers working over water-ways.
quotes: Other water creatures will only obey a summons if a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor of 6 + Creature Size is successfully made.

entries.title: Flame Dancers
entries.summary: Template for people possessed by the power of fire, with fire-related powers and compulsions.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Let the Bonfire Burn, Personal Power: Endurance of the Flame Dancer

entries.title: Forgotten Gods
entries.summary: Template for old gods who survive in living form, built around a Focus or Greater Power describing their sphere of influence.
quotes: As characters, they should take a Greater Power or Focus Power that describes this influence.

entries.title: Loamwalkers
entries.summary: Template for tree-spirits living in human shape, with powers to travel between trees and change between tree and human form.
quotes: Common Flaws: Dark Secret (Loamwalker), Essential Flaw (minor): Antisocial (Presence), Fear (fire), Baneful Circumstances (must be rooted into the earth)

entries.title: Men of the Lake
entries.requires: Magic kin: Man of the Lake
entries.summary: Template for sentient lake beings with water powers, a seasonal society and a network of lake regiones.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Drown (see page 137), Personal Power: Simulacrum Form, Ritual Power: Command the Waters, Focus Power: Memory of Water, (Lake) Regio Network.

entries.title: Orphan Born
entries.summary: Template for humans conceived beyond the veil of the spirit world, who can become incorporeal and see spirits.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Incorporeal Form, Personal Power: Ghostly/Physical Form, Second Sight

entries.title: People of the Clouds
entries.requires: Magic kin: Person of the Clouds
entries.summary: Template for sky-sailors who command the wind and can fly or sail ships through the air.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Sail the Wind

entries.title: The Stoneskinned
entries.summary: Template for people of living rock whose stone powers scale with age or Might and who turn to stone in daylight.
quotes: These stats are Init +X, Atk +2X, Dfn +X, Dam +2X, where X is either the character's (Might Score / 5) or his (age / 10).

entries.title: Warders of Mystery
entries.summary: Template for the society of Auditores who keep magic secret, with a power to perceive distant places through Arcane Connections.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Perceive the Distant Truths

entries.title: Spirits as Characters
entries.summary: Spirits are incorporeal, immortal beings that cannot affect or be sensed by matter without powers or magic, communicating through Silent Speech, and take the Magic Spirit Virtue.

entries.title: Spirit Concept
entries.summary: How to set Characteristics for spirits, that Size is meaningless until a spirit takes physical form, and that all spirits have the Magical Air Flaw.
quotes: For plants and spirits of non-living objects, assume that all Characteristics begin at zero and apply 7 characteristic points in the usual fashion.

entries.title: Spirit Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Which seasons suit different kinds of spirits and why spirits often take Reduced Abilities.

entries.title: Spirit Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Spirits need no Quality to be incorporeal or immortal, but need Powers to be seen or to affect the world, so most of their Qualities go to Powers.

entries.title: Daimons
entries.summary: Daimons, the Named Spirits, remain in the Magic Realm and act on Earth only through short-lived Aspects with their own Might, which are constant Arcane Connections to the parent.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.

entries.title: Dragon-Born (Magic Kin)
entries.summary: Explains dragon-born human offspring of zmajevi as a type of Magic Kin who buy Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws at character generation and can be identified with Second Sight.
quotes: Dragon-born are another type of Magic Kin

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.89 Magic Kin

entries.title: Dragon-Born Statistics
entries.summary: Gives the Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws for dragon-born characters, requires a Personal Power mirroring the dragon parent's powers, and offers example powers.
quotes: Greater Immunity (fire)
A dragon-born character receives a Personal Power

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic Realm p.41 Personal powers

entries.title: Character Guide: A Sibyl (magic character template)
entries.requires: Being type: Magic Human / Magic character
entries.summary: A minimal-statistics template for a sibyl built with the Magic Characters rules, with notes on the five points of Virtues and Flaws, Magic Might, and the Enigmatic Essential Trait that prevents her speaking clearly.
quotes: The sibyl's Enigmatic Personality Trait is an Essential Trait; magical effects to make her speak clearly mysteriously fail.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 7 (Divination & Augury)

entries.title: Blemmyae Characters
entries.summary: Describes the physical traits of Blemmyae and the Magic Qualities and Inferiorities they inherit as Magic Humans, with differences between male and female Blemmyae and notes on armor and shields.
quotes: Male Blemmyae also have the Age Quickly Major Flaw as a Magic Inferiority, meaning that they have a lifespan typical of that of a human.
They cannot use large shields effectively.

entries.title: Size, Might and Characteristics of Elementals
entries.summary: A table giving an elemental's Size and its eight Characteristics for each Might score from 1 to 50, used when designing a new elemental.
quotes: The Size of an elemental is dependent on the Might chosen for it, and the Might of an elemental also determines its typical Characteristics.

alsoIn.title: Size, Might, and Characteristics of Elementals

entries.title: Elemental Powers
entries.summary: Every elemental has a power from its elemental matter and a power describing its natural attack, plus usually one more. Its natural attack costs no Might points, so its Penetration is typically its Might.
quotes: the elemental does not need to spend Might points for this attack, meaning that its Penetration for this is typically equal to its Might.

entries.title: Earth Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Crush power every earth elemental has (pinning and breaking equipment) and optional powers such as The Red Touch and Slake Thirst, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All earth elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Water Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Drown power every water elemental has and optional powers such as Chill Touch and Sight of the River, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All water elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Air Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Sufficiale suffocation power every air elemental has, including the contested Quickness + Athletics roll to escape, plus optional powers such as Dissolution and Jupiter's Touch.
quotes: All air elementals have the following power:
Compare Quickness + Athletics stress rolls of the victim and the elemental (using Might/5 for the elemental's Athletics), the highest wins.

entries.title: Fire Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Burn power every fire elemental has (damage from a stress die plus its current Might pool) and optional powers such as Fascination and Heat of the Searing Forge.
quotes: All fire elementals have the following power:
takes damage equal to a stress die plus the entity's current Might pool

entries.title: Designing Elementals
entries.summary: Introduction to building an elemental character as a Magic Thing, with its inherited Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: the general principles can be applied to use an elemental as the starting point for a magic character

entries.title: Elemental Concept and Characteristics
entries.summary: How an elemental's Size and element determine its Characteristics, which Characteristics cannot be negative for each element, and the Size adjustment applied to Quickness and Strength.
quotes: make the usual adjustment from Size, subtracting Size from Quickness and adding twice Size to Strength.

entries.title: Elemental Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Elementals are normally Spring characters and must buy Brawl and Athletics (or Swim for water) to a score tied to their Might, using Improved Abilities if experience runs short.
quotes: Elementals are almost always Spring characters

entries.title: Elemental Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Elemental Might is set by the amount of matter it formed from and fixes its Size, with fixed free Qualities and an obligatory Greater Power for its element.
quotes: Every increase in magnitude of Might (as if it were a spell) adds three to the Size.

entries.title: Siren Song (Seirenes)
entries.summary: A Major Virtue letting the character command those who hear her music, resolved as a Communication + Music roll against the target's Stamina roll with a bonus table by command severity. Limits help from other musicians and explains how it combines with Enchanting Music.
quotes: A successful roll of Communication + Music versus the target's Stamina roll allows the character to issue a command to any individual or group who hears the music
No more than two musicians' scores can assist the singer in performing a song

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Guidance on spending Might on Magical Qualities, with powers restricted to those that express the species' perfection.
quotes: determine its Might and spend these points on Magical Qualities, taking Magical Inferiorities if you want more points to spend

entries.title: Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: Describes the cloud regio of Nephelococcygia, how to enter it, and the Inherited Virtues and Flaws of the intelligent birds who live there.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Homing Instinct, Keen Vision, Lightning Reflexes.
an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: The set of Greater Powers available to Birds of Nephelococcygia, each given with its Hermetic guideline breakdown.

entries.title: Cat Character Template
entries.summary: A worked template showing how to build a magical cat character from the mundane stats and magical additions.
quotes: Cats may only have 10 points of Qualities
Might divided by 5, rounded up

entries.title: Cats as Example
entries.summary: Explains that the cat section is a model for building power lists for other species, borrowing powers and following the same guidelines.

entries.title: Black Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Black Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: White Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the White Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Tortoiseshell Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Tortoiseshell Lineage, its rare males, and its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Cat Magical Powers
entries.summary: Each purchase of a Greater or Lesser Magical Power Quality gives a cat one power chosen from the lists.
quotes: Players designing cats select one magical power for each purchase of the Greater Magical Power or Lesser Magical Power Qualities.

entries.title: Cats' Greater and Lesser Powers
entries.summary: Rules for the spell-level cost, Penetration Score, Might cost and Initiative Bonus of cat powers.
quotes: A Penetration Score = Might of the cat (5 x the cost of the power) + the cat's Penetration Bonus.
The Initiative Bonus for a Lesser Power is equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude x 2).

entries.title: Personal Magical Powers for Cats
entries.summary: Rules for the Initiative bonus, spell-level cost and Penetration Score of personal powers for cats.
quotes: An Initiative bonus equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude /2).

entries.title: Dragons as Characters
entries.summary: Weak dragons can be built with the magical character rules as grogs, companions or magus-equivalents, while non-player dragons need not be strictly balanced.

entries.title: Dragon Concept
entries.summary: Base Characteristics, Size, required Virtues and suggested Virtues and Flaws when designing a dragon or dragon-kin.
quotes: Dragons and their kin have base Characteristics of 0, and 7 points to spend on improving Characteristics (like human characters).

entries.title: Dragon Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which seasons suit serpents and dragons and on giving combat opponents a good Brawl.

entries.title: Dragon Might Score and Qualities
entries.summary: A table of typical Might ranges for each kind of dragon-kin, plus advice on Qualities for breath, gaze and combat statistics.
quotes: A dragon's combat statistics may be improved through liberal use of the Improved Attack, Improved Defense, Improved Damage, and Improved Soak Qualities.

entries.title: Designing Giants
entries.summary: Humanoid beings larger than human size get their Size from the Gigantic Quality.

entries.title: Giant Concept
entries.summary: Story roles and suggested Virtues and Flaws for giants, which use the Magic Human rules with the Gigantic Quality applied after Characteristics.
quotes: Giants should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4.

entries.title: Giant Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Spring giants suffer child-like Characteristic penalties and language Abilities must be bought with the giant's season experience.

entries.title: Giant Might and Qualities
entries.summary: All giants take the Major Quality Gigantic, repeated for larger Sizes, which drives the Might needed.
quotes: All giants must take the Major Quality, Gigantic; giants larger than Size +2 should take it more than once.

entries.title: Giant Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Giants use clubs, with combat statistics computed normally allowing for the Gigantic Quality's effects.

entries.title: Non-Human Giants
entries.summary: To build oversized elementals, spirits or animals, use the rules for that creature type and add the Gigantic Quality.
quotes: simply choose Gigantic as one of the creature's Qualities

entries.title: Spirit Votary (Virtue and Character Type)
entries.summary: A Free Supernatural Virtue making the character a Mythic Companion who must take Spiritual Pact plus further supernatural Virtues and the Pagan Flaw.
quotes: A Spirit Votary is required to take the Spiritual Pact Virtue (see below), along with either three Minor Supernatural Virtues or one Major Supernatural Virtue.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.103 Blood of Heroes

entries.title: Designing Revenants
entries.summary: Revenants are usually Spring or Summer Magic Humans with the No Fatigue and Improved Soak Qualities to reflect their resilience.
quotes: They should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4: Magic Characters.

entries.title: Powers of the Spirits
entries.summary: Introduces common spirit powers, which must penetrate Magic Resistance, with Ritual-like powers permanently reducing the spirit's Might.
quotes: Naturally, any power that affects another being must penetrate its Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Ghosts as Characters
entries.summary: Ghosts are built as spirits with the Magic Spirit Virtue, and the ability to take material form is treated as a supernatural power that not every ghost has.
quotes: are spirits with no true material form and must have the Magic Spirit special Virtue

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Concept
entries.summary: Steps for building a ghost: choose a Flaw as its worldly tie, generate Characteristics as for a human, give it Magic Spirit and a Magical Social Status, and drop Virtues and Flaws that no longer apply.
quotes: All ghosts should have the special Virtue, Magic Spirit

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which character Season to use for apparitions, shades and spectres according to how much of their living knowledge they retain.
quotes: should usually be designed as Autumn characters.

entries.title: Quick Ghost Conversion (ka)
entries.summary: A step-by-step kit for turning an ordinary character into an Egyptian ghost (ka): choose Magic Might, swap Virtues and Flaws, add Magic Spirit, note intangibility and vulnerability to Mentem, and add powers and vis.
quotes: Give the character a Magic Might score of between 5 and 25
Add vis, usually Mentem, equal to the Might score divided by 5.

entries.title: Quick Animated Statue Conversion
entries.summary: A kit for building an animated statue from a mortal character, including Soak by statue material, size adjustments to Strength and Quickness, damage penalties for stone or bronze weapons, and how to force a ghost out of a statue.
quotes: Wood grants +9 Soak.
Hard metal grants +21 Soak.
Characters lose 2 Strength and gain 1 Quickness per Size lost, or conversely gain 2 Strength and lose 1 Quickness per Size gained.

entries.title: Royal Pharaonic Ghosts
entries.summary: Guidelines for designing the ghosts of Egyptian royalty: bloodline Virtues from Faerie gods, odd powers drawn from a pharaoh's life, and Transformation after death thanks to long death rituals.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Transformation

entries.title: Drowned Men Characters
entries.summary: Drowned Men must take the Transformed (Being) Virtue and commonly have a sea Flaw, Greater Immunity (drowning) and the Servant of the Ocean Flaw.

entries.title: Homunculi Wizards
entries.requires: Flaw: Homunculus Wizard (character with The Gift)
entries.summary: Explains hedge wizards who gain a faerie version of The Gift through a bond with a homunculus: what they can do, their dependence on feeding and hiding the homunculus, and how to build one as a character.
quotes: To play a Homunculus Wizard as a character, take The Gift and the Homunculus Wizard Flaw during character creation.

related.text: House Merinita outer mystery of Faerie Magic

entries.title: Creating Golems
entries.requires: Ability: Kabbalah; studied the Sefer Yetzirah
entries.summary: Creating a golem takes several seasons: shape clay, then accumulate points toward its Might with an Awaken Golem Total, with a Might cap, botch dice and a limit of one golem per protected community.
quotes: AWAKEN GOLEM TOTAL: Intelligence + Kabbalah + Wonders + Ceremony Bonus + Dominion Aura
AWAKEN GOLEM EASE FACTOR: 30
MIGHT CAP: Kabbalah x 5

entries.title: Standard Golem Traits
entries.summary: Starting attributes for a human-form golem played as a Companion: free Characteristics, fixed Virtues and Flaws, starting Abilities and Personality Traits, and a True Name that cannot change.
quotes: All golems have the Unaging and Improved Characteristics Virtues.
Golems do have a True Name, which is determined during their creation.

entries.title: Spiritual Pact (Major Supernatural Virtue)
entries.summary: Extended rules for a character bound by pact to a Magic spirit: spending a Confidence Point to draw a temporary Might pool, how Penetration and duration work, the lack of a Might score, and how the spirit's own pool is reduced.
quotes: Make a Presence + Magic Lore + stress die roll: this is the amount of Magic Might Pool that the character acquires from his spiritual master.
A character can only have a single pact.

entries.title: Mythic Blood: Gigantes (Greek giants)
entries.summary: A Mythic Blood lineage for descendants of the Greek giants with snake tails, listing the typical Magical Focus, Personality Flaw and common Virtues and Flaws, plus two new Flaws (Rebellious and Horrifying Appearance - Snake Legs).
quotes: The Magical Focus that accompanies the Mythic Blood is usually connected with strength or the Form of Terram, and the Personality Flaw is Rebellious.

entries.title: Faerie Virtues and Flaws (Cognizance, Wards, Faerie Sight and Speech)
entries.summary: Explains the faerie-specific traits used to build faeries: regeneration without fatigue, degrees of Cognizance, Faerie Sight, Faerie Speech, and Traditional and Sovereign Wards that harm or exclude a faerie.
quotes: Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
Direct contact with a sovereign ward destroys the body of a faerie, removing it from the scenario.
The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.

versions.title: Faerie Virtues and Flaws
versions.summary: Explains that a Supernatural Virtue can be designated as having a Faerie origin, which gives it the Faerie bonuses on the Realm Interaction Table and spares the character Warping from living in a Faerie aura; notes Benediction and Malediction as typical faerie gifts and curses.
quotes: characters with a Faerie Virtue or Flaw do not gain Warping from living in a Faerie aura.
related: ArM5 pp.54-55 Greater and Lesser Malediction

entries.title: Designing Faerie Characters: Sequence of Choices
entries.summary: Overview of the order of decisions for creating a faerie: player or non-player, power level, Might, physical form, cognizance, role, powers and vulnerabilities.
quotes: Faeries are designed through a series of choices.

entries.title: Faerie Characters: PC or NPC
entries.summary: Non-player faeries may be more powerful than new player characters and need not balance Virtues and Flaws; the bestiary uses these rules as examples but troupes may design more informally.
quotes: Non-player characters do not need to balance their Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Faerie Level of Power
entries.summary: A player faerie should be about as powerful as a companion or magus, and the troupe should agree on the design so that it does not reduce others' enjoyment.
quotes: approximately as powerful as a companion or magus

entries.title: Faerie Virtues, Flaws and Pretense Points
entries.summary: A player faerie replacing a companion or magus gets a limited allotment of Virtues balanced by Flaws, and a pool of Pretense points set by the average magus age; inherent Abilities of the physical form must be bought first.
quotes: 1 free, then up to 20 points of Virtues paid for with Flaws at 2 Virtues per Flaw.
(average age of magus player characters – 5) + 120 points
which gives 360 points of Pretences

entries.title: Required Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
entries.summary: Every faerie character needs a Might score, physical form, level of cognizance, Social Interaction Virtue and a taboo; innate powers can be traded away as Flaws.
quotes: A character must have a Might score, a physical form, a level of cognizance, a Social Interaction Virtue, and a taboo.

entries.title: Faerie Might Score and Might Points
entries.summary: Sets a starting Might score for player faeries, gives innate Magic Resistance equal to Might, and explains that Might Points are spent on powers and recover steadily over a day; notes that Might varies widely with role.
quotes: Player characters begin with a Faerie Might score of 5
Faerie Might gives the character innate Magic Resistance equal to its Might Score.
Faeries have Might Points equal in number to their Might score, which they spend to activate their powers.

entries.title: Quick Start Guideline (Faerie Characters)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving a fast recipe for a companion-level faerie: a stated Might, Characteristics and Pretence points, a short list of Virtues, free choices and a Traditional Ward Flaw.
quotes: has a Faerie Might of 10
360 Points of Pretences: Spend them exactly like Ability points.

entries.title: Faerie Physical Form: Ageing and Fatigue
entries.summary: Explains what a faerie body is and its advantages: no ageing or Decrepitude unless a Flaw says otherwise, no Fatigue, and great difficulty in dying.
quotes: Faeries cannot age or suffer Decrepitude unless they have a Flaw.

entries.title: Equipment Without Encumbrance
entries.summary: A faerie carries traditional props of its role without Encumbrance and can reconstitute a lost prop for no Might in a round.
quotes: Reconstituting a prop costs no Might, and requires a single round.

entries.title: Faerie Regeneration and Rebuilding a Body
entries.summary: Faeries heal by cognizance level, and a faerie killed before humans rebuilds a body in a time set by its Might and the local aura; memory and role changes after rebuilding depend on cognizance.
quotes: The time taken to regenerate equals the faster of the Faerie Might Score in months or Faerie Might Score / Aura (as modified by the Realm Interaction Table) in months.

entries.title: Scale of Typical Might Scores
entries.summary: Sidebar table giving descriptive Might bands from ordinary creatures to earth-shaking figures with example bestiary faeries at each level.
quotes: | 1–10 | An ordinary creature of a realm. |

entries.title: Faerie Human and Animal Forms
entries.summary: How to build Characteristics for humanoid and animal-form faeries, and how animal-form player faeries swap Cunning for Intelligence as a free Virtue.
quotes: A humanoid faerie has 7 points with which to buy Characteristics
This is a Free Virtue.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, Book of Mundane Animals
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Hybrid Forms and Natural Weapons
entries.summary: Hybrid forms are human forms with animal elements that are cosmetic or Minor Virtues; faeries' natural weapons use Brawl and a table of Init, Atk, Dfn and Dmg values and need no Virtue.
quotes: This uses the Brawl Ability and the statistics on the following table.
Having natural weapons does not, in itself, require a Virtue.

entries.title: Glamorous, Immaterial Forms
entries.summary: Immaterial faeries are invisible and pass through solid objects but must take on matter to move things; design them as the physical body they don, with the Intangible Flesh Flaw.
quotes: Immaterial faeries are invisible to those without magical aid, and can pass through solid objects.

entries.title: Faerie Size
entries.summary: Humanoid faeries choose a Size with required Strength and Quickness adjustments; extreme sizes need troupe scrutiny, and nonhuman characters adjust Characteristics only if they deviate more than one from their base Size.
quotes: Characters outside the range of Size +2 to –3 are difficult to accommodate in sagas, and should be carefully scrutinized by the Troupe.
Characters deviating from their base size by 1 do not change Characteristics, but those deviating by more than 1 are adjusted as indicated by the table above.

entries.title: What Do Size Scores Represent?
entries.summary: Reference table of Size scores from tiny to huge with height, weight, comparison creature and the wound-penalty ranges for each Size.
quotes: | Size | Height | Weight | Comparison | Wound Penalties |

entries.title: Faerie Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Faeries take Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws that cover only dealings with humans and replace Social Status Virtues; with other faeries a player faerie is treated as a representative of its human companions.
quotes: govern only their interaction with humans and replace Social Status Virtues

entries.title: Faerie Cognizance in Character Design
entries.summary: A faerie's cognizance shapes its goals and limits how it can develop new powers: low-cognizance faeries do not consciously improve, middling ones transform predictably, and highly cognizant ones can change roles between scenes.
quotes: Characters of low cognizance do not consciously attempt to improve their statistics during the saga.

entries.title: Unspecialized Role (Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities)
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling that faeries can have Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities without the Virtues humans need, though professionals quickly detect the fraud.
quotes: Faeries do not require the Virtues that allow characters to have Martial, Arcane, or Academic Abilities to have Pretenses for them.

entries.title: Faerie Taboos: Traditional and Sovereign Wards
entries.summary: Faerie taboos are built from Ward Flaws: a Traditional Ward bars touching the ward, stops Might regeneration and burns the faerie as a damage source, while a Sovereign Ward bars harming the protected person and destroys the faerie's body on touch.
quotes: The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.
Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
the faerie may not harm a person or thing that is defended by the ward

entries.title: Folk Charms (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A faerie with this taboo cannot face folk charms deliberately used against it, whatever the culture; personal charms precious to a human also serve and are Arcane Connections to that human.
quotes: A character with this taboo cannot face folk charms, deliberately used, from any culture

entries.title: Herbs (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: The herbs that repel a faerie depend on its role and the herb's underlying symbolism; identifying the right herb needs Faerie Lore or the ability to read the faerie's glamour.
quotes: The herbs that repel a faerie are based on that faerie's role, so the faerie is unable to vary them, except by changing roles.

entries.title: Iron (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Iron is a common faerie ward, and some faeries refuse to deal with those carrying it, while miners, crafters and urban faeries are often comfortable with it.
quotes: Some faeries refuse to negotiate with humans who carry iron, even if they will not suffer from contact with it

entries.title: Names (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A character who knows the name of a faerie with this taboo can force it to leave him alone, so powerful faeries use titles and roles instead.
quotes: If a faerie has this taboo, and a character knows its name, the character can force the faerie to leave it alone.

entries.title: Payment or Thanks (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Some faeries must leave human service once paid or thanked, either because the relationship is balanced or their story is complete, and a few then turn on their former employers.
quotes: Some faeries must leave human service if paid or thanked.

entries.title: Places (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Place-based taboos must seriously inconvenience the faerie, for example foreign earth acting as a Traditional Ward, and a Sovereign Ward tying a faerie to its home makes it unsuitable for most player characters.
quotes: Flaws based on places must seriously inconvenience the character.
Characters tied to their home with a Sovereign Ward simply cannot leave, and are unsuitable as player characters in most sagas.

entries.title: Religious Symbols (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Faeries with this taboo flee symbols such as church bells; many powerful faeries also cannot enter the Dominion without God's invitation.
quotes: Many of the most powerful faeries cannot enter the Dominion, because God has not invited them in and they are unable to trespass.

entries.title: Inappropriate Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
entries.summary: Lists which Virtues and Flaws a faerie character may never take (Gift, Hermetic, Divine/Infernal powers, human social status and upbringing) and what to take instead.
quotes: Faeries may not have The Gift, or any Virtue or Flaw specific to Hermetic magi.
If the faerie has a role that makes it appear part of human society, it should take the Infiltrator Virtue.

entries.title: Faeries and Confidence
entries.summary: Faeries have no Confidence scores; the Reputation as Confidence Virtue gives them false Confidence points to back up their Reputations.
quotes: Faeries do not have Confidence scores.
A faerie with this Virtue gains a number of false Confidence points equal to its highest reputation

entries.title: Faerie Personality Flaws
entries.summary: Sets how many Personality Flaws a faerie may take, noting that role-linked Flaws are often required.
quotes: Faeries may have up to three Minor Personality Flaws and one Major Personality Flaw

entries.title: Focus Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie a themed, spontaneous-style power built from a pool of spell levels, with Might cost and Initiative set by the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The player receives 25 spell levels to spend on this power.
an initiative score of (the character's Quickness – the power's maximum magnitude)

entries.title: Greater Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers designed at character creation, with a reduced Might cost and Initiative penalty compared to Lesser Powers.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 50 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)

entries.title: Lesser Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers; cheaper to acquire than Greater Powers but each use costs more Might and is slower.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 25 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each effect's Might Point cost is equal to the magnitude of the effect.

entries.title: Personal Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie a single Personal-range spell-like power designed like a formulaic spell.
quotes: Personal powers must have Personal Range.

entries.title: Intricacy Points
entries.summary: Intricacy points let a faerie make a power faster or cheaper in Might, and can be gained from unspent spell levels or the Improved Powers Virtue.
quotes: Every 5 unspent levels equal an intricacy point.

entries.title: Odd Targets and Durations
entries.summary: Allows faerie powers to use Merinita Ranges, Targets and Durations, and defines the Until Duration and dual Durations.
quotes: In this book it is treated as being equivalent to Year, but not requiring a Ritual.

entries.title: Faerie Power Virtue Comparison Table
entries.summary: Table comparing spell levels, effect type, Might cost and Initiative for each faerie power Virtue.
quotes: Qik – maximum magnitude

entries.title: Ritual Power
entries.summary: Major Virtue for ritual-level faerie effects, which cost Might Score as well as Might points whenever they are used.
quotes: All Ritual Powers are at least Level 20, regardless of the actual level of the effect
The Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2).

entries.title: Improved Powers
entries.summary: Minor Virtue granting intricacy points to a faerie's powers, or optionally mastery-like abilities for them.
quotes: This Virtue gives the character 5 intricacy points to spend on any of its powers.

entries.title: Constant Powers
entries.summary: Rules for making a Greater, Lesser or Personal Power constant, triggering at every sunrise and sunset.
quotes: costs an additional magnitude

entries.title: Powers of Transformation
entries.summary: Advice on which faerie power Virtue to use when designing transformation powers, depending on whether specific or varied substances are involved.
quotes: then that is best designed as a Greater Power

entries.title: Focus Powers
entries.summary: Intro to Focus Powers: broad themed effects whose Might cost and Initiative follow the magnitude produced, to be agreed with the troupe.
quotes: Each use of a focus power has a Might Point cost equal to the magnitude of the effect

entries.title: Power Design: An Example
entries.summary: Worked example of designing faerie powers from Hermetic spells, choosing between Personal, Greater, Lesser and Focus Powers and spending intricacy points.
quotes: Personal powers cost (magnitude/2) points, rounding up

entries.title: Pretense: Faerie Abilities
entries.summary: Explains that faeries use Pretenses in place of Abilities, and that few faeries can teach humans, especially those linked to the dead.
quotes: Some exceptional faeries are able to teach Abilities to humans.

entries.title: Faerie Instructor and Faerie Trainer
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Instructor or Faerie Trainer
entries.summary: Virtues allowing a faerie to teach humans, either by trading stored Abilities or by training with conventional methods.
quotes: The faerie imparts the Ability by trading it for the Ability that the student currently has.

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretenses
entries.summary: Pretenses tied to a faerie's story role rather than a human Ability must be negotiated with the troupe.
quotes: These player-defined pretenses must be negotiated with the troupe.

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretense Example: Chivalrous Combat
entries.summary: Worked example of negotiating a broad player-defined Pretense with a built-in limitation.

entries.title: Why Isn't My Faerie a Genius At Every Ability?
entries.summary: Explains why starting faerie characters lack great experience, including how and when faeries lose Pretenses.
quotes: Faeries often lose Pretenses.

entries.title: Varieties of Faerie Blood
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood
entries.summary: Lists specific kinds of Faerie Blood (bloodcap, brownie, dwarf, ettin, faerie god, ghul, goblin, huldra, nymph, padfoot, satyr, selkie, sidhe, undine), each with its benefit, an enhanced benefit for Faerie Legacy, typical Sympathies, suggested Virtues and Flaws, and appearance.
quotes: Note that this enhanced effect replaces the normal benefit of Faerie Blood, it is not in addition to it.

entries.title: Faerie Powers for the Faerie Blooded
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood (storyguide option)
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a character with Faerie Blood take a restricted list of faerie-only Virtues and Flaws, paying Might costs of their powers in Fatigue rather than Might points.
quotes: instead of spending Might points, the character instead loses 1 Fatigue level for every 5 points (or fraction) of the cost
assume that the character has a Might Score of zero

entries.title: Faerie Upbringing (Changelings)
entries.summary: Explains children raised among faeries, who have the Faerie Upbringing Flaw and usually Faerie Blood, and gives the list of Abilities from which a character with this background has an Ability Block.
quotes: Choose any five Abilities from the following list as unavailable to a character with this Flaw: Animal Handling, Charm, Church Lore, Dominion Lore, Etiquette, Folk Ken, Guile, Leadership, Ride, Theology

entries.title: Linked Lives
entries.requires: Exchanged with a troll or trowie changeling
entries.summary: Describes a human whose life is bound to the faerie changeling left in his place, represented by Faerie Blood, possibly Faerie Upbringing, and the Death Prophecy Virtue, with a Faerie Friend or Mistaken Identity relationship.
quotes: that the character can only die if his faerie copy is killed first

entries.title: Milk Brothers
entries.summary: Describes the bond between a human who has shared milk with a gwiber and the creature: the Animal Ken Virtue and the Faerie Friend Flaw rather than Faerie Blood.

entries.title: Nympholepts
entries.summary: Describes mortals taken to live with nymphs for years, who gain Faerie Blood effects plus often a prophetic power such as Premonitions, the Visions Flaw or the Faerie Power of Dream.

entries.title: Generic Minor Vila (template and power-conversion notes)
entries.summary: Template for a weak generic vila usable as a grog-level antagonist or player character, with notes on buying powers as Greater or Lesser Powers, Personal Powers and a quick-play option for faerie power costs.
quotes: Troupes preferring speed over accuracy should double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the powers given here.

entries.title: Role-Specific Vila Powers (customizing by role)
entries.summary: Explains how to build a vila for a story role, balancing added Virtues with Flaws for a player character, and how the Ostentatious and Pretentious Virtues give extra pretense points.
quotes: The first adds 10 times the average age of the PC magi points to the character's pool of pretense points. The second adds 5 times the average age of the PC magi points.

entries.title: Bee King (Strong Faerie Blood variety)
entries.requires: Virtue: Strong Faerie Blood (Bee King variety)
entries.summary: Describes the special powers of a Bee King: commanding bees, speaking with hives, immunity to biting insects, and treating attacking bee swarms as an automatic damage effect rather than a melee group, along with the fixed lifespan drawback.
quotes: An attacking bee swarm is treated as an environmental effect, rather than an opposing mêlée group.

entries.title: Sympathy Traits of the Olympians
entries.summary: Table of the positive and negative Sympathy Traits for each Olympian god, for characters taking the Faerie God variant of Faerie Blood.
quotes: Characters taking the Faerie God variant of Faerie Blood

entries.title: Societas Merceris: the Bloodcaps
entries.requires: Redcap society: Bloodcaps (Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood, plus a Malediction)
entries.summary: A Redcap society of faerie-blooded border guards; members must take Faerie Blood and a Greater or Lesser Malediction triggered by the cross or scripture, and tend to carry combat-oriented magic items.
quotes: All Bloodcaps must take Faerie Blood (or Strong Faerie Blood)

entries.title: Pagan Traditions
entries.summary: Introduces faerie hedge wizard traditions, with Favored Abilities that are easier to learn, Initiation Scripts, and the minimum Virtue points and Sympathy Traits needed to build a starting faerie wizard.
quotes: the player must devote at least four points of the character's starting Virtues to a Faerie Method and a Faerie Power

related.text: Chapter 5: Touches of Faerie, Learning Supernatural Abilities

entries.title: Character Guide: Stoicheion (faerie guardian template)
entries.summary: A faerie character template with its Virtue and Flaw budget and powers, including the Guardian of the Bounds ward power with its Might cost and the Extended Glamour vis yield.
quotes: The power costs 1 Might point per 5 levels (or fraction) of the equivalent spell.
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of Animal vis, which manifests as physical objects within the controlled region.

entries.title: True Faith
entries.summary: True Faith is measured by a Score and Faith Points that work like Confidence, and the Score gives Magic Resistance; Faith Points are regained each dawn up to the Score.
quotes: TRUE FAITH MAGIC RESISTANCE: True Faith Score X 10
Each dawn, you regain a number of Faith Points up to your True Faith Score

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, p.56

alsoIn.title: Taking the True Faith Virtue (Faith Score and Points)

versions.title: True Faith (overview)
versions.summary: Explains what True Faith is, who can hold it, and that it is represented by a Major Virtue, a True Faith Score and Faith Points. A character with it can pray for miracles and gains magical resistance, and on death is invested with Divine Might.
quotes: invested with Divine Might (equal to his True Faith Score multiplied by 10)
Only living people may have True Faith.

entries.title: Example of Creating a Devout Character
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious
entries.summary: A worked example of assigning starting Devotion Points to saints for a pious lay character, including the extra Devotion Points a relic can grant.

entries.title: Devotion
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious (or the Pious Personality Flaw)
entries.summary: Introduces Devotions to particular saints as a Divine-aligned Ability-like statistic bought with separate Devotion Points rather than ordinary experience, and gives the character-generation rule for how many Devotions and Devotion Points a pious Christian starts with.
quotes: Devotions advance as an Ability, but do not use normal, generalized Experience Points, instead relying on a dedicated form of experience points called Devotion Points.
may spend Devotion Points equal to the positive score in that trait to establish Devotions

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

versions.title: Devotion (True Faith 2)
versions.summary: At the stated Score the character gains Premonitions and can dispel any supernatural illusion or Faerie glamour by spending a Faith Point.
quotes: the character may dispel any supernatural (magical and Infernal) illusion or Faerie glamour, no matter its level, by spending a Faith Point

entries.title: Increased Faith (higher True Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Sidebar on creating characters with a True Faith Score above the basic one; each extra point of Score costs a further Major Virtue and such characters should be Mythic Companions.
quotes: Each additional increase to the character's True Faith Score above that granted by the True Faith Virtue is considered a Major Virtue.

entries.title: Personality Traits, Sins, and Tempers
entries.requires: Divine-aligned characters and mystics (Sinful Traits and Tempers)
entries.summary: Groups Personality Traits into paired Sins and Tempers, lets a trait be annotated with its Sin or Temper, and explains that a trait's value counts negatively for the opposed one.
quotes: When dealing with opposing tempers or sins, treat the trait's value as negative.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40 Sins and Tempers

entries.title: Mystics (female religious)
entries.requires: Visions Flaw, or True Faith with the Understanding power
entries.summary: Explains how to represent a religious mystic in game terms: usually the Visions Flaw, or occasionally True Faith with Understanding and Meditation. Also covers how a bishop's (or pope's) acceptance of a nun's visions earns her a Reputation as a mystic.
quotes: In most case, the experiences of a religious mystic are covered by the Visions Flaw.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.34, 36, 37, 54

entries.title: Joining the Franciscan Tradition
entries.summary: How a character becomes a member of the Franciscan tradition, either at character creation (supernatural Virtues balanced by Flaws, with Monastic Vows compulsory) or in play through an invitation from a Mystagogue.
quotes: the Supernatural Virtues that bestow the favored Abilities must be balanced by Flaws in the conventional manner, and Monastic Vows is compulsory.

entries.title: Banishing (Donatores)
entries.summary: A Supernatural Accelerated Ability that expels creatures of one realm from a designated area for a Sun duration, with an Ease Factor depending on area size and a re-entry roll for the banished creature that reduces its Might. Includes a worked example.
quotes: Banishing Total: stress die + Presence + Banishing + aura
the default Ease Factor is Near Range, which is defined as the area within 10 paces of the character
Stamina + (Realm) Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 12

related.text: ArM5 p.148 Weight of a Thousand Hells
RoP: The Infernal p.34 True Names

entries.title: Holy Tradition: Sufis
entries.summary: Describes the Sufi holy tradition, its favored Abilities and its group dhikr and sama' meditation rituals, whose benefits are boosted by a shaykh's Ceremony Ability.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Ceremony, Meditation, Transcendence, Understanding
their shaykhs will often possess the Ceremony Ability, which enables them to synchronize their efforts in order to reach higher degrees of understanding.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Blessed by God, New Abilities (Ceremony)

entries.title: Holy Societas: Zoroastrians
entries.summary: Describes the Zoroastrian holy societas of Magoi, including favored Abilities, taboos of purity, and its link to Holy Magic and Hermetic House Flambeau.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Invocation, Holy Magic, Sense Holiness and Unholiness, Wonders
These spells require Holy Magic to cast and are only taught to members of the tradition.

entries.title: Holy Tradition: Ba'al Shem
entries.summary: The tradition of itinerant Jewish folk magicians who make amulets and give blessings, with its favored Abilities and note that Initiations grant extra Methods and Powers.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Adjuration, Blessing, Craft Amulets, and Invocation

entries.title: Holy Societates: Karaites
entries.summary: Describes Karaite Gifted magi who may join the Order if their magic is Holy Magic; lists required Flaws and favored Abilities, and the restriction on taking apprentices.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Craft Amulets, Holy Magic, Merkavah, Transcendence
Hermetic Karaites can only take Gifted apprentices from within their own religion.

entries.title: Holy Tradition: Hesychasts
entries.summary: Gives the favored Abilities of ascetic and monastic hesychasts for the Holy Tradition rules, and notes their proneness to Divine Gloom.
quotes: Meditation, Purity, Transcendence, Understanding
Ceremony, Meditation, Transcendence, Understanding

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, page 63 (Divine Gloom)

entries.title: Society of Cyprian and Justina
entries.requires: Tradition: Holy Society of Cyprian and Justina
entries.summary: Gives the favored Abilities of this Holy Society of repentant magicians who serve the Divine.
quotes: Favored Abilities: Holy Magic, Invocation, Sense Holy/Unholy and Wonders

entries.title: Initiation into the Entreat the Divine Powers Ability
entries.requires: Initiation: Entreat the Divine Powers (unGifted mathematicus)
entries.summary: Initiation Script granting the Entreat the Divine Powers Minor Virtue after a season of service with a Divine Lore test, with the Flaw gained.
quotes: Script Bonus: +14 (+3 Quest, +9 Major Ordeal, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sympathetic Bonus)

entries.title: Creating Muslim Characters
entries.summary: Muslim characters are made as normal, but some Virtues and Flaws are forbidden or renamed, extra ones are available, and two new Academic Knowledges are added.
quotes: Muslim characters, be they rural or urban in origin, are generated in the same way as other characters.

entries.title: Strangers in Foreign Lands (Non-Muslims and Muslims abroad)
entries.requires: Character living across the Muslim/non-Muslim divide
entries.summary: Non-Muslims under Muslim rule generally must take a status Flaw and are barred from some classes, while Muslims living in non-Muslim lands must take an Outsider-type Flaw.
quotes: Almost all non-Muslim characters living under Muslim rule must also take the Minor General Flaw Dhimmi
they should always take the Major Social Status Flaw Outsider

entries.title: Forbidden Virtues for Muslim Characters
entries.summary: Lists the Social Status Virtues that Muslim characters may not take because the institutions do not exist in Muslim lands.
quotes: Magister in Artibus (European-style universities do not exist in Muslim lands)

entries.title: Forbidden Flaws for Muslim Characters
entries.summary: Lists the Flaws that are not available to Muslim characters because their situations do not arise in Muslim societies.
quotes: Branded Criminal (Criminals are not branded in Muslim societies)

entries.title: Islamic Law and Theology: Islam (Abilities)
entries.requires: Muslim character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: Two Academic Knowledges used by Muslim characters: Islamic Law, the Muslim counterpart of Civil & Canon Law, and Theology: Islam, the counterpart of Christian Theology, each with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law.
This is the Islamic equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Judaic Lore (Ability)
entries.summary: A Knowledge of Jewish cultural practice such as poetry, folklore and songs, which all Jewish characters have to some degree and may take from childhood experience.
quotes: All Jewish characters are versed in Judaic Lore to some degree

entries.title: Rabbinical Law (Ability)
entries.requires: Jewish character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: The Jewish version of Civil & Canon Law, with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Jewish version of Civil & Canon Law.

entries.title: Theology: Judaism (Ability)
entries.requires: Jewish character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: The Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology, with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Virtues Forbidden to Jewish Characters
entries.summary: Explains which Social Status and other Virtues Jewish characters cannot take, and that they must take Educated (Hebrew) to gain Academic Abilities.
